items.extension: I also became more careful about keeping copies of important files. That way, an unexpected computer problem would be less stressful in the future.

items.question: Describe an advertisement with a famous person in it
items.questionZh: 描述一则有名人出演的广告。
cueCard: And explain how you feel about the advertisement
cueCardZh: 并解释你对广告的感受
items.answer:
An advertisement I remember features Michael Jordan, the basketball player. It's an old Nike video about failure, and versions of it can still be found online. I came across it at home while looking at basketball videos on my phone.

What interested me was the message. Instead of only showing a famous player winning, the advertisement connects success with making mistakes and continuing to try. The product isn't the part that stayed in my mind. It was the idea that even someone people admire has experienced failure.

I liked that because I sometimes feel embarrassed when I make a mistake on the basketball court. My friend has encouraged me in that situation, so the message felt personal. Of course, watching an advertisement doesn't suddenly make me a better player. Still, it reminded me to focus on the next chance instead of the last mistake. I found it more memorable than an advertisement that simply tells me to buy something.

items.question: Describe a place you have travelled to that you would like to recommend to others
items.questionZh: 描述一个你去旅行过、想推荐给别人的地方。
cueCard: What you saw and did there
And explain why you would like to recommend it to others
cueCardZh: 你在那里看到、做了什么
并解释为什么想推荐给别人
items.answer:
A place I'd recommend is Dadonghai Beach in Sanya, which is in Hainan. I went there with my girlfriend, and it's a place I remember mainly because of how relaxed I felt.

The seawater was clear, and I really enjoyed the sea breeze. We walked slowly along the beach without trying to follow a busy schedule. I also took lots of photos of my girlfriend. We tried a few different angles, but we weren't in a hurry to get a perfect picture. Just spending time together was enjoyable.

What I liked most was being able to take a break from my usual routine. As a student, I spend quite a lot of time looking at a computer screen, so the open space felt refreshing. I'd recommend it to someone who enjoys the sea and wants a simple, relaxing trip. You don't need to plan an expensive activity to have a good time there.

items.extension: If I went again, I'd leave enough time for another slow walk. That's the part I remember most clearly, along with taking photos and enjoying the view.

items.topic: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
items.question: Describe a home that you like to visit but do not want to live in
items.questionZh: 描述一个你喜欢拜访、但不想住进去的家。
cueCard: Why you like to visit it
And explain why you would not like to live there
cueCardZh: 并解释为什么不想住在那里
items.answer:
A home I enjoy visiting but wouldn't want to live in is my grandfather's house in a village in Hainan. It's a fairly simple house with a small outdoor area where he grows plants.

When I visit, we usually sit together, have something to eat and talk. Sometimes I help him water the plants. The pace of life feels slower there, and I enjoy having time away from schoolwork and computer screens. I also like seeing the small things he has made or repaired around the house.

However, living there every day would be less convenient for me. It's far from my school and the places where I normally meet my friends. Travelling back and forth would take too much time. So my feelings about the house depend on the situation. It's a lovely place for a short family visit, but at this stage of my life, I'd prefer to live somewhere closer to my daily activities.

So my feelings about the house depend on the situation. It's a lovely place for a short family visit, but at this stage of my life, I'd prefer to live somewhere closer to my daily activities.
cluesZh: 地点外观：海南村里的爷爷家，简单房子，带种植物的小户外空间。
拜访的乐趣：一起吃东西聊天、浇花，看爷爷制作修理的小物件；节奏慢，暂离功课和屏幕。
不想长期住的原因：离学校和朋友活动地远，来回费时；适合短暂家庭拜访，但当前生活更需要便利。
translationsZh: 不过，每天住在那里对我来说就不太方便。它离学校和我通常见朋友的地方都远，来回会花太多时间。所以，我对这所房子的感受取决于情境。短时间去看家人时，它是个很好的地方；但在人生现阶段，我更愿意住在离日常活动近的地方。
items.provenance: 沿用拟写爷爷人物：海南村里有小院的家；位置、到访活动及交通不便均待调整，不当作真实家庭情况。
items.extension: That doesn't mean I dislike the area. I just think a place that is perfect for a quiet weekend may not suit my everyday routine.

items.question: Describe a story/book with animals in it
items.questionZh: 描述一个包含动物的故事或一本书。
cueCard: And explain what you think of this story/book
items.answer:
A story with animals that I remember is The Tortoise and the Hare. I read it in a collection of Aesop's Fables that I borrowed from a library. I chose the book because the stories were short and easy to follow.

The main animals are a tortoise and a hare, which is similar to a rabbit. They have a race. The hare runs much faster and becomes so confident that it stops to rest. Meanwhile, the tortoise keeps moving slowly and eventually reaches the finish first.

I like the story because its message is simple without being useless. It reminds me that starting well isn't enough if you stop making an effort. I can connect that with learning English. Some people learn more quickly than I do, but regular practice can still help me improve. The story doesn't suggest that speed is always bad. To me, it's more about taking a task seriously and continuing until it's finished.

情节：乌龟和野兔比赛，兔子快却自信到停下休息，乌龟持续慢行先到终点。
观点与应用：道理简单却实用，开局好不等于能放弃努力；联系英语学习，快不坏，重点是认真坚持到完成。

items.provenance: 龟兔赛跑的情节为已有寓言；在图书馆借阅《伊索寓言》、选择理由和读后联系为拟写，与 N27 一致。
items.extension: I also like how easy it is to remember the two animals. Their different ways of behaving make the lesson clearer than a long explanation would.

items.question: Describe a person who solved a problem in a smart way
items.questionZh: 描述一个巧妙解决问题的人。
cueCard: And explain why you think he/she did it in a smart way
cueCardZh: 并解释为什么你认为方法巧妙
items.answer:
A person who solved a problem in a smart way was my friend Leo. We were working on a small website for a university class, and he was responsible for the part that allowed users to sign in.

At one point, that part didn't work properly. We could have kept changing different things and hoping for the best, but Leo suggested checking one small part at a time. He wrote down what should happen and compared it with what actually happened. That helped him narrow down where the problem was.

When he still needed help, he showed our teacher a clear example instead of simply saying that the website was broken. With that advice, he fixed the problem. I thought his approach was smart because it made a confusing task manageable. He didn't pretend to know everything, and he didn't waste time guessing. I learned that asking a clear question can be part of solving a problem well.

排查方法：登录异常时不乱改，而是逐项检查，记录预期与实际结果，缩小问题范围。
求助与评价：拿清楚例子问老师后修好；把混乱任务变得可处理，不装懂不瞎猜，清楚提问也是解决能力。

items.provenance: 沿用 N02 的三人网站项目和 Leo 解决登录问题；属于专业背景下的新增经历，不挪用你的电脑清灰故事。
items.extension: I have tried to use the same approach in my own work since then. Breaking a problem into smaller parts makes it feel less stressful.

items.question: Describe a law on environmental protection
items.questionZh: 描述一项环境保护法律法规。
cueCard: How you first learned about it
And explain how you feel about this law
items.answer:
An environmental law I know about is Hainan's rule restricting certain single-use plastic products that do not break down naturally. It took effect in December 2020. It doesn't mean that every kind of plastic product is banned.

I first became interested in it after noticing information about shopping bags when I was out shopping. Later, I looked up a short explanation online. Since I live in Haikou, it felt connected to daily life rather than being a distant issue.

I think local residents, visitors and wildlife can all benefit if the rule helps reduce plastic waste. Hainan has beaches that people enjoy, and keeping rubbish out of the sea matters to me. I feel positive about the aim, although people need practical alternatives. For example, bringing a reusable bag should be easy and affordable. A rule works better when people understand what they should do and can follow it without too much difficulty.

cluesZh: 规定与范围：海南限制部分不能自然降解的一次性塑料制品，2020 年 12 月生效；不是禁止所有塑料。
了解途径：购物时注意到购物袋相关信息，之后网上查简要说明；住海口，感觉与日常生活相关。
受益与条件：减少垃圾有利居民、游客和野生动物，保护海滩大海；赞同目标，但要有方便可负担的替代用品及清楚说明。
translationsZh: 我知道的一项环保规定，是海南限制部分不能自然降解的一次性塑料制品的规定。它在 2020 年 12 月生效。这并不意味着每一种塑料制品都被禁止。
我认为，如果规定有助于减少塑料垃圾，当地居民、游客和野生动物都能受益。海南有大家喜欢的海滩，避免垃圾进入海洋对我很重要。我认同这个目标，不过人们需要切实可行的替代品。例如，自带可重复使用的袋子应该方便、也负担得起。当人们理解该做什么，并能较容易地遵守时，一项规定就能更好地发挥作用。

items.provenance: 法律事实：海南相关规定于 2020-12-01 起实施，限制名录内的一次性不可降解塑料制品，并非禁止一切塑料。通过购物提示了解及个人反应为拟写。
items.extension: I would explain it to a friend using everyday examples, such as shopping bags. That seems more useful than trying to remember complicated legal terms.

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: Describe a time when you sent a message or an email to someone but received no reply for a long time
items.questionZh: 描述一次你发消息或邮件后，很久没有收到回复的经历。
cueCard: Whether you finally received the reply
And explain how you felt about the experience
cueCardZh: 并解释你对这次经历的感受
items.answer:
A time I waited quite a while for a reply was when I sent my friend Leo a message about playing basketball. I wanted to know whether he was free that weekend, because I needed to arrange my study time around it.

I sent the message in the afternoon and expected a fairly quick answer. However, nothing came through that evening. I checked my phone several times and started wondering whether he had seen it. I didn't want to keep sending messages, though, because the plan wasn't urgent.

He finally replied the next morning. He explained that he had been busy and that his phone had run out of battery. We were still able to arrange the game, so there wasn't a serious problem. I felt relieved and a little silly for checking so often. The experience reminded me that a slow reply doesn't necessarily mean someone is ignoring me. Sometimes people simply have other things to deal with.

cluesZh: 对象目的：发消息问 Leo 周末是否有空打篮球，好安排学习时间。
等待过程：下午发，期待快回，晚上却没收到；反复查手机，因不紧急而没有不断催。
结果与反思：次晨回复，原来忙且手机没电，仍能约球；放心又觉得多虑，慢回不一定是忽视。
translationsZh: 他终于在第二天早上回复了。他解释说，之前一直很忙，手机也没电了。我们仍然约成了球，所以没出什么大问题。我松了口气，也觉得自己老看手机有点傻。这次经历提醒我，回复慢并不一定意味着别人不理我。有时，人们只是有别的事情要处理。
items.provenance: Leo 为球友代称；发消息约周末篮球、等到第二天、朋友忙且手机没电等为拟写，不当作已经发生。
items.extension: Now, if I need an answer by a certain time, I say that clearly in the message. It helps the other person understand what I need.

items.question: Describe a long-term goal/ambition you would like to achieve
items.questionZh: 描述一个你希望实现的长期目标或抱负。
cueCard: How long you have had this goal/ambition
And explain why you set it
items.answer:
A long-term goal I have is to become a software developer who can build useful things. I've had this goal since I started studying computer science at university, although my ideas about the future are still developing.

To work towards it, I need to understand the basics well and practise regularly. I don't think just watching lessons is enough. I want to finish small projects, get feedback and learn how to fix my mistakes. Working with classmates can also help me explain my ideas more clearly.

I set this goal because I like the feeling of solving a problem and seeing something work. For example, even a simple program can save someone time if it does a useful job. I don't expect to become an expert quickly, and I know some parts will be difficult. Still, this goal gives my studies a clear purpose. I'd feel proud if something I built made another person's daily life a little easier.

实施办法：打好基础、经常练习，不只看课；完成小项目、求反馈、改错，并在合作中练表达。
原因与意义：享受解决问题、让程序运行，实用小程序也能省时间；不求迅速精通，但目标让学习有方向，想帮助别人。

items.provenanceType: 真实专业背景加目标草稿
items.provenance: 计算机专业为真实；成为软件开发者、大学以来的目标和练习计划未确认，可按真实职业打算调整。
items.extension: Improving my English is part of that plan too, because it could help me understand more learning materials and communicate with people from different places.

items.question: Describe a time when you changed an important opinion of yours
items.questionZh: 描述一次你改变重要观点的经历。
cueCard: And explain how you felt about the experience
cueCardZh: 并解释你对这次经历的感受
items.answer:
An important opinion I changed was my idea of success. I used to connect success mainly with becoming rich or famous. That began to change after I watched King of Comedy at home with my parents.

At first, I mainly enjoyed Stephen Chow's humour. But what stayed with me afterwards was the idea of an ordinary person continuing to try even when other people didn't believe in him. It made me think about why people keep working towards something when there is no guarantee of a big result.

I started to feel that success could also mean making steady progress and not giving up on a life you care about. You don't have to become an important public figure for your effort to matter. This change made me feel less pressure when I compared myself with others. I still want to do well, but now I'd rather focus on improving step by step than expect one huge achievement to prove my value.

电影启发：起初欣赏周星驰的幽默，后来记住普通人不被看好也坚持；思考没有辉煌结果保证时为何仍努力。
新观点与影响：成功也可以是持续进步、不放弃在意的生活；不必成大人物，减少比较压力，用逐步改进而非巨成就证明价值。

items.provenance: 真实：在家与父母看《喜剧之王》，欣赏幽默及普通人的坚持。补充：此前将成功等同名气、看完后改变该观点；时间未具体化。
items.extension: That idea also helps with English practice. A difficult day doesn't mean all my work is useless; it just means I need to keep going.

items.question: Describe an environmental law you would like your country to introduce
items.questionZh: 描述一项你希望国家推行的环保法律。
cueCard: Why people should follow the law
Whether the law will be popular
And explain how you feel about this law
items.answer:
An environmental law I'd like to see introduced more widely would require large public parks and busy beaches to provide safe drinking-water refill points. The aim would be to make carrying a reusable bottle more convenient.

People should follow the rule because it could help reduce the number of empty plastic bottles thrown away. Of course, simply putting a machine somewhere wouldn't be enough. The people responsible would need to keep it clean, check the water and repair it when necessary.

I think the idea would be popular with visitors because they could save money and avoid carrying several bottles. Some places might worry about the cost, so starting with a few busy locations would be sensible. I feel positive about this kind of law because it gives people a practical way to change a small daily habit. As someone who enjoys walking by the sea, I'd like it to be easier for everyone to leave less rubbish behind.

I feel positive about this kind of law because it gives people a practical way to change a small daily habit. As someone who enjoys walking by the sea, I'd like it to be easier for everyone to leave less rubbish behind.
cluesZh: 提议与目的：大型公园和繁忙海滩提供安全饮用水补水点，让自带可重复使用水瓶更方便。
遵守理由与落实：减少丢弃塑料瓶；不只安装机器，负责人还要清洁、检查水质并维修。
受欢迎程度与评价：游客省钱、少带水瓶，但场所担心费用，可先试点；通过可行方法改变小习惯，减少海边垃圾。

items.provenance: 与 R06 共用安全饮水补水点的制度建议；属于希望推广的设想，不声称所有地方都没有类似规定或设施。
items.extension: Clear signs would help too. If visitors couldn't find the refill point, even a well-maintained machine would do little to change their buying habits.

items.question: Describe a piece of local news that people are interested in
items.questionZh: 描述一则人们感兴趣的当地新闻。
cueCard: And explain why people were interested in it
cueCardZh: 并解释为什么人们感兴趣
items.answer:
A piece of local news that attracted people's attention was the introduction of Hainan's restrictions on certain single-use plastic products. The rules took effect in December 2020, so this is an older news story, not something that happened this week.

I read an online report about it while looking for information on the environment in Hainan. The story involved local authorities, shops and ordinary residents, because changing the kinds of bags and other products people use affects daily shopping.

I think people were interested for different reasons. Some wanted to know what they would need to bring when shopping, while businesses needed to understand which products were covered. Others cared about reducing waste near the sea. Living in Haikou, I found the topic easy to relate to. It showed me that local news can be about small changes in daily habits as well as major events. I also discussed the idea of carrying a reusable bag with my family.

Others cared about reducing waste near the sea. Living in Haikou, I found the topic easy to relate to. It showed me that local news can be about small changes in daily habits as well as major events. I also discussed the idea of carrying a reusable bag with my family.

关注原因：居民想知道带什么，商家需懂适用范围，也有人关心海边减废；联系海口生活并与家人聊环保袋。

items.extension: The useful part of a report like this is a clear explanation of what changes for ordinary people. Without that, the headline alone isn't enough.

items.question: Describe a change that you made recently
items.questionZh: 描述一个你最近作出的改变。
cueCard: What you did for the change
And explain how you feel about the change
cueCardZh: 并解释你对改变的感受
items.answer:
A change I made recently was setting a clear finishing time for playing computer games in the evening. I still enjoy games, but I realised that starting one more round could easily take time away from other things.

The main reason for the change was my English preparation. I wanted to practise speaking regularly, and waiting until I felt completely free wasn't working very well. So I began doing a short practice session before playing and deciding when I would stop in advance.

I kept the plan simple because a very strict schedule would be difficult for me to follow. Some evenings still go better than others, but I spend less time wondering when to begin. I feel happier with the balance now. Games remain something I look forward to, while studying feels more manageable. The change has shown me that I don't always need to give up an activity I enjoy; sometimes I just need clearer limits around it.

items.topic: 对结果开心的重要决定
items.question: Which is better, to make a decision quickly or slowly?
items.questionZh: 做决定快一点好，还是慢一点好？
items.answer: It depends on the consequences. Choosing lunch can be quick, because a poor choice won't matter for long. Choosing a university subject deserves more thought. Still, thinking slowly is only useful if people gather relevant information; worrying about the same thing repeatedly may not improve the decision.
items.ideaZh: 看后果大小：午餐可快选，专业要多考虑；慢想要伴随搜集信息，反复担忧无益。

items.topic: 对结果开心的重要决定
items.question: Do you think most people's decisions are made in their 20s?
items.questionZh: 你认为人们大多数决定都在二十多岁时做出吗？
items.answer: People often make major choices about study and work in their twenties, but I wouldn't say most decisions happen then. They continue making important choices about family, careers and where to live later on. A decision made at twenty also doesn't have to determine someone's whole life.

items.question: What if people in a group have different opinions on a decision?
items.questionZh: 团队成员对一个决定意见不同时怎么办？
items.answer: They should first agree on what they want to achieve. Then they can compare the options using the same priorities, such as cost or time. For a class project, trying a small version of each idea might help. If everyone just defends their own preference, the discussion can go nowhere.
items.ideaZh: 先统一目标和评判标准，再比较或小范围尝试方案，避免只维护个人偏好。

items.topic: 对结果开心的重要决定
items.question: What little decisions do people make every day?
items.questionZh: 人们每天会做哪些小决定？
items.answer: People decide what to wear, what to eat and how to travel. They also choose what to do first when they have several tasks. These decisions seem small, but repeated habits matter. Spending ten minutes planning a study session, for example, can make starting it much easier.
items.ideaZh: 穿衣、吃饭、出行和任务顺序都是小决定，长期习惯也有影响，学习规划可举例。

items.topic: 对结果开心的重要决定
items.question: Do you think it is a good idea to make a small decision every day?
items.questionZh: 每天作一个小决定是好事吗？
items.answer: Yes, making small choices can give people practice in judging options and accepting the result. Children might choose a book or plan a small purchase. I don't think people need to create extra decisions just for practice, though; ordinary daily life already offers plenty of opportunities.
items.ideaZh: 小选择能练判断和承担结果，但日常机会已足够，不用刻意增加决定。

items.topic: 对结果开心的重要决定
items.question: How can we tell the difference between an important and an easy decision?
items.questionZh: 怎样区分重要的决定和容易的决定？
items.answer: I'd look at how long the result lasts and how difficult it is to change. An important decision may affect health, money or other people. But important and easy aren't opposites. Sometimes a major decision feels easy because someone knows their priorities very clearly.
items.ideaZh: 看影响持续多久、能否改动；同时指出重要和容易不对立，目标清楚时大事也好选。

items.topic: 做困难事情并成功的人
items.question: In which sectors are companies more likely to succeed in China?
items.questionZh: 在中国，哪些行业的公司更容易成功？
items.answer: I wouldn't assume any sector guarantees success. I'd expect opportunities in services that solve everyday problems, such as useful software or support for older people. But even a promising idea needs customers who can afford it. How a company operates matters as much as the field it enters.
items.ideaZh: 不说某行业必成功；解决日常问题的软件或养老服务或有机会，仍要看需求与经营。

items.question: Is it easy to start up a company?
items.questionZh: 创办公司容易吗？
items.answer: Starting a small operation may be manageable, but keeping it running is much harder. Owners need to find customers, control costs and handle unexpected problems. Someone who cooks well, for example, still needs to understand pricing and service before a restaurant can become a stable business.
items.ideaZh: 开始小生意可能不难，持续经营更难；用餐饮举例说明还需客户、成本和服务管理。

items.question: Other than making money, what is more important for a company?
items.questionZh: 除了赚钱，公司还有什么更重要？
items.answer: Customer trust is extremely important, because income may not last if people feel disappointed or misled. Treating employees fairly matters too. A company needs enough money to survive, but reliable products and good working relationships can help it keep going beyond one successful sale.
items.ideaZh: 客户信任和公平对待员工很重要，有助于长期经营，而不只完成一次销售。

items.question: Does money equal success?
items.questionZh: 有钱就等于成功吗？
items.answer: Not necessarily. Money can make life more comfortable, but people may also value useful work, close relationships or progress towards a personal goal. A small business owner who earns enough and has satisfied customers could feel successful without becoming rich. It depends partly on what success means to that person.
items.ideaZh: 不一定；工作价值、关系和个人进步也重要，收入够用且顾客满意也可算成功。

items.question: How can companies help protect the environment?
items.questionZh: 公司如何保护环境？
items.answer: They can start by reducing waste in their normal operations, for example using less packaging and repairing equipment instead of replacing it too quickly. They should also check what happens to their rubbish. Clear, practical changes are more convincing than an advertisement that simply describes a company as green.
items.ideaZh: 从减少包装、维修设备和处理垃圾做起，具体改变比自称环保更可信。

items.question: Is it difficult to do business in today's world?
items.questionZh: 当今做生意困难吗？
items.answer: It can be difficult because businesses compete for attention and customers can compare options easily. On the other hand, online tools can help a small company reach people without opening many shops. The challenge is using those tools while still offering something customers actually want and can trust.
items.ideaZh: 竞争与比价增加难度，网络工具也降低触客门槛；关键是提供有需求且可信的产品。

items.question: When do you think people are happiest?
items.questionZh: 你认为人们什么时候最快乐？
items.answer: People often seem happiest when they feel connected to others and aren't under too much pressure. That might happen during a family meal or after finishing a difficult task. I don't think happiness always comes from a major achievement; small, enjoyable moments can make an ordinary day feel good.

items.question: How can the arts spread positive emotions in society?
items.questionZh: 艺术如何在社会中传播积极情绪？
items.answer: Music, films and performances can give people an experience to share. A comedy might help a family laugh together after a difficult day, while a song can express a feeling that is hard to explain. The effect depends on the audience, though; people don't all enjoy the same kind of art.
items.ideaZh: 电影音乐提供共享体验，也能表达难说的感受；效果因观众喜好而异。

items.question: Do you think teachers are able to spot the unhappy children?
items.questionZh: 老师能发现不开心的孩子吗？
items.answer: Sometimes, especially if they know a child's usual behaviour. A student who suddenly stops joining activities may need attention. But teachers can't know everything from appearances, because some children hide their feelings. A calm, private conversation is likely to tell them more than simply assuming what is wrong.
items.ideaZh: 熟悉孩子时可能看出变化，但不能只凭外表，私下平静交谈更有帮助。

items.question: Should teachers know what children are doing all the time?
items.questionZh: 老师应该随时掌握孩子在做什么吗？
items.answer: No, constant checking would be unrealistic and could make children uncomfortable. Teachers should know enough to keep students safe and support learning, while allowing some independence. Clear rules and regular conversations can help. The amount of supervision should also depend on the child's age and the situation.

items.question: What would make a student happy at school?
items.questionZh: 什么会让学生在学校开心？
items.answer: Feeling accepted by classmates makes a big difference. Students also need work they can understand with some effort and teachers who notice their progress. For example, a child who struggles with a subject may feel much happier after receiving useful help rather than being compared with the best student.

items.question: Do you think doing a job that you like is more important than other things?
items.questionZh: 做喜欢的工作比其他因素更重要吗？
items.answer: Enjoying a job matters because people spend so much time doing it. But pay, working hours and how colleagues treat each other matter too. I'd look for a reasonable balance. Even an interesting job can become unpleasant if someone is exhausted or cannot cover their basic living costs.

items.question: What should people wear to a job interview?
items.questionZh: 求职面试应该穿什么？
items.answer: They should wear something clean and suitable for the workplace. A formal office may expect smarter clothes than a casual technology company. The aim is to look prepared and feel comfortable enough to concentrate. Spending a lot on a new outfit doesn't necessarily make someone a stronger candidate.

items.question: Why do we need to attend interviews when applying for jobs?
items.questionZh: 申请工作为什么需要面试？
items.answer: An application shows qualifications, but an interview lets both sides ask questions. Employers can hear how someone explains a problem, and applicants can learn what the work is really like. It is most useful when the questions relate to the job rather than simply testing how confidently someone speaks.

items.question: What should people do to prepare for a job interview?
items.questionZh: 求职面试应该做哪些准备？
items.answer: They should understand the role and prepare a few clear examples of relevant experience. Practising answers can help, but memorising every sentence may sound unnatural. I'd also check the journey or the online connection beforehand, so a small practical problem doesn't create unnecessary stress on the day.

items.question: Why do some people think interviews are a waste of time?

items.answer: Some interviews repeat information already written in an application or ask questions that have little connection with the work. Candidates may also spend a lot of time preparing without receiving useful feedback. That frustration makes sense, although a well-planned interview can still help both sides make a decision.

items.question: Why do some people dislike being interviewed?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人不喜欢接受面试或采访？
items.answer: They may feel nervous about being judged or struggle to explain themselves under pressure. Someone can be good at a job without being a confident speaker. Unclear questions make this worse. A friendly introduction and a little thinking time can help people give a more accurate picture of their abilities.

items.question: What kinds of people are usually interviewed?
items.questionZh: 哪些人通常会接受面试或采访？
items.answer: Job applicants are a common example. Journalists also interview public figures, experts and ordinary people who have experienced an event. items.question: Do you think it is important for managers to be well organized?
items.questionZh: 管理者做事有条理重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, because a manager's organisation affects other people's work. If tasks or deadlines are unclear, a whole team may waste time. Being organised doesn't mean planning every minute. It means making priorities clear, sharing information and adjusting the plan when something important changes.

items.question: Should parents teach their children to be organized?
items.questionZh: 父母应该教孩子做事有条理吗？
items.answer: Yes, but they should teach it through simple routines rather than constant criticism. A parent could help a child choose a place for school things and prepare a bag the night before. As the habit becomes familiar, the child can take more responsibility without needing reminders every time.

items.question: What can people do to become more organized?
items.questionZh: 人们怎样变得更有条理？
items.answer: They can begin with a short list of priorities and a regular place for important things. Keeping the system simple matters, because a complicated plan is easy to abandon. For students, checking tomorrow's tasks at the end of the day can prevent a rushed start the next morning.

items.question: Are organized people more likely to be successful at work or in their studies?
items.questionZh: 有条理的人更容易在工作或学习中成功吗？
items.answer: Organisation can improve their chances because they are less likely to forget tasks or leave everything until the deadline. However, they still need relevant skills and effort. A beautifully arranged timetable won't help much if the person never actually starts the work or asks for help when they are stuck.

items.question: Do you think children should learn to be organized from a young age?
items.questionZh: 孩子应该从小学习有条理吗？
items.answer: Yes, as long as the expectations match their age. A young child can learn to put toys back, while an older child can plan homework. These habits develop gradually. Expecting a child to manage a full adult-style schedule would probably create frustration rather than useful independence.

items.question: Why is it important for people to be organized?
items.questionZh: 有条理为什么重要？
items.answer: It reduces the time people spend searching for things or worrying about forgotten tasks. That leaves more attention for the work itself. For example, clear folders can make a group project easier to manage. Organisation should support daily life, rather than become another task that takes too much time.
items.ideaZh: 减少找东西和担心漏事的耗时，让人专注任务；整理应服务生活，不额外添负担。

items.question: How can people consider others' feelings when chatting in public?
items.questionZh: 在公共场所聊天时如何顾及别人？
items.answer: They can lower their voices and notice the setting. A lively conversation is more acceptable in a busy market than in a library. If a call will be long or personal, stepping away from others is helpful. People don't need complete silence everywhere, but they should pay attention to those nearby.

items.question: How would people usually respond to noises in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家的人通常怎样应对噪声？
items.answer: It varies. Some people put up with ordinary street noise, while others move away or politely ask for the volume to be lowered. If noise continues late at night, they may contact whoever manages the building. I wouldn't say there is one response shared by everyone in the country.

items.question: Which area is exposed to noise more, the city or the countryside?
items.questionZh: 城市还是农村更容易受到噪声影响？
items.answer: Usually cities, because traffic, construction and businesses are close together. The countryside can be noisy too, with machinery or animals, but the sounds may be less constant. The exact location matters: a quiet city street could be more peaceful than a house next to a busy rural road.

items.question: What kinds of noises are there in our life?
items.questionZh: 生活中有哪些噪声？
items.answer: There are transport sounds, building work, music and people's conversations. At home, appliances can add background noise as well. Whether a sound feels annoying depends partly on what we're doing. Music might be enjoyable during a break but distracting when we're trying to concentrate on a difficult task.

items.question: Should children not be allowed to make noise under any circumstances?
items.questionZh: 是否任何情况下都不应允许孩子发出噪声？
items.answer: No, that would be unreasonable. Children need to talk, laugh and play, and those activities naturally make some noise. They should learn that different places have different expectations. Running and shouting may be fine in a playground, while a library requires a quieter voice.

items.question: Do you think it is good for children to make noise?
items.questionZh: 孩子发出噪声是好事吗？
items.answer: Some noise is a normal part of playing and expressing excitement. It can show that children are involved in an activity. But they also need to learn how their behaviour affects others. The goal should be suitable places and clear limits, rather than treating all noise as either good or bad.

items.question: Which is more important, protecting the environment or developing the economy?
items.questionZh: 环保和经济发展哪个更重要？
items.answer: I don't think they can be separated completely. People need jobs, but damaged surroundings can also make life and business harder in the long run. I'd support development that considers its environmental cost from the beginning, such as protecting green space when planning new housing, instead of trying to repair everything later.

items.question: Do you think staying in a natural place would help change people’s mood?
items.questionZh: 待在自然环境里能改变心情吗？
items.answer: It can help, especially when someone has spent a long time indoors. A quiet walk gives them a change of scene and a break from screens. It won't remove every problem, of course. But simply having space to breathe and notice the surroundings can make a stressful day feel more manageable.

items.question: Do you think there should be many natural places in cities?
items.questionZh: 城市里应该有很多自然空间吗？
items.answer: Yes, and they should be spread across the city rather than gathered in one distant area. People are more likely to visit a small nearby park regularly. Green spaces also need care and suitable paths, because a neglected place may not feel welcoming even if it has plenty of trees.

items.question: What can governments do to encourage people to spend more time in nature?
items.questionZh: 政府怎样鼓励人们多接触自然？
items.answer: They can make parks easy to reach and pleasant to use, with clear paths, shade and places to sit. Free activities may introduce people to a local green space. Keeping these places clean matters too. Encouragement works better when an outdoor visit is convenient for ordinary daily life.

items.question: Do you think people should spend more time in nature?
items.questionZh: 人们应该多花时间亲近自然吗？
items.answer: Generally, yes, particularly people who spend most of the day inside. Even a short walk can provide a useful change of routine. The amount depends on someone's circumstances, though. A nearby park is a realistic option for many people who don't have time for a long trip into the countryside.

items.question: What kind of people do you think enjoy being in nature?
items.questionZh: 哪些人喜欢亲近自然？
items.answer: All sorts of people can enjoy it, including families, photographers and people who want quiet time. Their activities may differ: some like a challenging walk, while others prefer sitting by the sea. I wouldn't connect enjoying nature with one age group or personality type.

items.question: Should people spend time on charity, or just money?
items.questionZh: 做慈善应该投入时间，还是只捐钱？
items.answer: Both can be valuable. Money helps organisations buy supplies, while volunteers can offer practical support or useful skills. People should consider what the organisation actually needs and what they can reliably provide. A small regular contribution may be more helpful than a big promise that someone cannot keep.

items.question: What kind of things do people usually save money for?
items.questionZh: 人们通常为了什么存钱？
items.answer: People save for different things depending on their stage of life. A student might save for headphones or a trip, while a family may save for housing or education. Some also keep money for unexpected costs. Having a clear purpose can make it easier to delay smaller purchases.

items.question: Is it easier to spend money or save money?
items.questionZh: 花钱还是存钱更容易？
items.answer: For many people, spending is easier because the reward is immediate. Saving means saying no to something now for a later benefit. But income matters too; someone with very little left after basic expenses may find saving difficult even if they are careful and have good habits.

items.question: Do you think it is easier to teach teenagers how to manage money when they are around 16 or 17 years old?

items.answer: In some ways, yes. Teenagers at that age can understand prices and plan purchases that matter to them. Giving them a small budget lets them practise. However, basic ideas can be introduced earlier, and age alone doesn't make learning easy; they still need clear examples and room to make small mistakes.

items.question: Should parents teach their children to spend money freely or to save money?
items.questionZh: 父母应教孩子自由花钱还是存钱？
items.answer: They should teach a balance. Children need to understand saving for future needs, but also how to spend sensibly on things they value. If spending always feels wrong, money becomes a source of unnecessary worry. A small allowance can help them practise choosing instead of buying everything immediately.

items.question: Should schools teach children how to manage money from a young age?

items.answer: Yes, using simple, practical activities. Younger children could compare prices or plan how to use a small pretend budget. Older students could discuss needs, wants and saving goals. Lessons should fit their age, because complicated financial language is less useful than habits they can apply in everyday life.

items.answer: It depends on the skill and the learner. Children may be more willing to try without worrying about looking foolish, while adults can use previous experience and clearer goals. items.question: What kinds of things do the elderly remember for a long time?
items.questionZh: 老年人会长期记住哪些事？
items.answer: Important relationships and major changes may stay with them for a long time, such as school days, starting work or raising children. A familiar song or place can also bring back an old memory. Still, older people are individuals, and we shouldn't assume they all remember or value the same things.

items.question: What sports are popular among older people?
items.questionZh: 哪些运动受老年人欢迎？
items.answer: Walking, gentle exercise and activities like table tennis may appeal to older people because they can be social and adjusted to different abilities. Some older adults enjoy much more demanding sports too. I think personal interest and fitness matter more than assuming everyone over a certain age wants the same activity.

items.question: What do old people usually do in their daily life?
items.questionZh: 老年人日常通常做什么？
items.answer: It varies with their health, interests and responsibilities. Some still work, some care for family, and others spend time on hobbies or meeting friends. A retired person might enjoy gardening or walking, but retirement doesn't mean everyone has the same routine or unlimited free time.
items.ideaZh: 视健康、责任和兴趣，有人工作、照顾家人或发展爱好，退休不等于都有很多空闲。

items.question: Why is there a generation gap between the young and the old?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与老人为什么有代沟？
items.answer: Different generations grow up with different technology, expectations and experiences. That can affect how they see work, relationships or spending money. Problems grow when each side assumes its own experience is the only normal one. Listening to the reasons behind an opinion can make the gap easier to understand.
items.ideaZh: 成长时的技术、期望与经历不同；双方只认自己的经验会加剧问题，倾听有帮助。

items.question: Has old people's life quality improved when compared to the past?
items.questionZh: 与过去相比，老年人的生活质量提高了吗？
items.answer: In some ways it may have, with more tools and services that make daily life convenient. But the improvement is not equal for everyone. Someone who feels isolated or struggles with digital services may still face difficulties. I'd consider independence, relationships and access to help, rather than just material comfort.

items.question: What can young and old people learn from each other?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与老人能互相学什么？
items.answer: Young people can learn practical experience and patience from older people. Older people may appreciate help with newer technology or a different view of current life. It should go both ways. For example, a grandparent could teach a useful cooking skill while a grandchild explains how to organise photos on a phone.

items.question: How can we tell if a listener is listening carefully?
items.questionZh: 怎样判断听众是否认真听？
items.answer: A careful listener usually responds to the actual point and asks relevant questions. They may briefly explain what they understood to check it. Eye contact can help, but it isn't proof on its own. Someone could look interested while thinking about something else, so the response matters more.

items.question: What would happen if the listener didn’t listen carefully?
items.questionZh: 听众不认真听会怎样？
items.answer: They might miss an important detail or misunderstand what they are expected to do. In a group project, that could mean completing the wrong task and wasting time. It can also make the speaker feel ignored. Asking for clarification early is usually easier than fixing the result of a misunderstanding.

items.question: What kind of topics do young people like to talk about today?
items.questionZh: 现在年轻人喜欢聊哪些话题？
items.answer: Among people I know, common topics include study, games, films and plans for the future. Friends also talk about everyday problems and funny things they've seen online. Interests vary, of course. A group of basketball fans may spend much more time discussing a match than another group would.

items.question: Can consumption drive economic growth?
items.questionZh: 消费能推动经济增长吗？
items.answer: It can, because spending gives businesses income and may encourage them to employ people or produce more. But the quality of that growth matters. Buying useful services is different from creating large amounts of waste, and people shouldn't feel they must spend beyond their means just to support the economy.
items.ideaZh: 消费带来收入和雇佣机会，但应重视增长质量，不鼓励浪费或超出经济能力消费。

items.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of shopping online?
items.questionZh: 网购有哪些优缺点？
items.answer: Online shopping makes it easy to compare prices and order without travelling. The main drawback is that you can't check the product directly before buying. A pair of shoes might look good in a photo but feel uncomfortable. Delivery and returns can also take more time than expected.

items.question: What are the differences between online shopping and in-store shopping?
items.questionZh: 网购和实体店购物有什么区别？
items.answer: Online shopping offers convenience and a wide range of choices, while a physical shop lets people see, touch or try the item. Shops can also provide immediate help from staff. My choice would depend on the product: a familiar basic item is easier to order online than something where fit matters.

items.question: Why do some people not like shopping in small shops?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人不喜欢在小店购物？
items.answer: They may expect fewer choices or worry that returns will be difficult. Some people also prefer browsing without close attention from a shop assistant. That doesn't mean small shops always give poor service. A friendly local shop can actually offer more useful personal advice than a much larger store.

items.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of shopping in small shops?
items.questionZh: 小店购物的优缺点是什么？
items.answer: A small shop may offer personal service and know what regular customers need. It can also be convenient for a quick purchase. However, it may have less space for different products and fewer staff at busy times. Whether it works well depends on the particular shop and what someone wants to buy.

items.question: Why are shopping malls so popular in China?
items.questionZh: 为什么商场在中国受欢迎？
items.answer: I think one reason is that people can combine shopping, eating and meeting friends in the same place. Indoor space is comfortable when it's very hot or raining. Some visitors may buy very little; they are using the mall as somewhere convenient to spend a few hours together.

items.question: Does art, like music or theater, have an impact on society?
items.questionZh: 音乐、戏剧等艺术对社会有影响吗？
items.answer: Yes, it can give people shared experiences and new ways to think about familiar issues. A play might help an audience understand another person's situation, while music can bring people together at an event. The effect isn't always immediate or the same for everyone, but art can influence conversation and feelings.

items.question: Is it good to have creative people in a team?
items.questionZh: 团队里有创意的人是好事吗？
items.answer: Yes, because they may suggest approaches that other team members haven't considered. However, a useful team also needs people who test ideas and finish the work. Creativity works best when members listen to each other, rather than treating every new suggestion as automatically better than the existing plan.

items.question: What impact can artistic buildings have on society?
items.questionZh: 艺术性建筑对社会有什么影响？
items.answer: They can make an area distinctive and give people a place they recognise or enjoy visiting. However, appearance alone isn't enough. A public building also needs to work well for the people using it. An impressive design is less successful if basic things like entrances and walking routes are inconvenient.

items.question: Do children these days still like doing arts and crafts?

items.answer: Some certainly do, especially when the activity lets them make something of their own. Screens compete for their attention, but that doesn't mean practical activities have lost all appeal. The materials and guidance matter. A simple project with room for choice may be more enjoyable than copying a perfect model exactly.

items.question: Why do some children enjoy making things by hand?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些孩子喜欢动手制作？
items.answer: They can see a clear result of their effort, which is satisfying. Making things also lets them choose colours, shapes or uses instead of following only one answer. A child who makes a small gift may feel proud because the object is personal, even if it doesn't look professionally made.

items.question: Do you think art classes are important for children?
items.questionZh: 艺术课对孩子重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, they give children a chance to explore ideas and practise looking carefully. Art can also provide a different way to express feelings. The classes shouldn't only reward the neatest picture. If children feel free to experiment and improve, more of them can benefit from taking part.

items.topic: 和朋友度过的愉快夜晚
items.question: Why do people need friends?
items.questionZh: 人们为什么需要朋友？
items.answer: Friends give people company, support and someone to share experiences with. A friend may understand a worry differently from a family member because they are at a similar stage of life. Friendship is also about enjoying ordinary things together, such as a meal or a game, rather than only asking for help.

items.question: Do older people prefer spending time with family or with friends?
items.questionZh: 老人更喜欢和家人还是朋友相处？
items.answer: It depends on their relationships and daily routine. Some older people enjoy being with children and grandchildren, while others value friends who share their interests. They shouldn't have to choose only one. Family can provide a sense of belonging, and friendship can offer a different kind of company.

items.answer: Many young people enjoy being with friends because they share interests and want more independence. That doesn't mean family becomes unimportant. items.answer: Younger people may choose activities connected with school friends or newer forms of entertainment. Older people may have more established routines and interests. items.question: What can we do to bring family members closer together?
items.questionZh: 怎样让家人关系更亲近？
items.answer: Regular time together helps, especially when people are paying attention instead of looking at separate screens. A shared meal or short walk gives everyone a chance to talk. items.question: How do people get along in a big family?
items.questionZh: 大家庭成员怎样和睦相处？
items.answer: They need clear communication and some respect for personal space. Sharing chores fairly can prevent small frustrations from building up. In a large family, people won't agree on everything, so being able to discuss a problem calmly matters. Spending time together is easier when nobody feels ignored or given too much work.

items.question: Why do some people refuse to abide by rules?

items.answer: Some people don't understand the purpose of a rule, while others find it inconvenient or think it won't be enforced. A few may believe their own situation deserves an exception. Clear explanations can help, but rules also need to be reasonable and applied fairly so that people take them seriously.

items.question: What kinds of things make people feel pressured?
items.questionZh: 什么事情让人感到压力？
items.answer: Deadlines, money worries and other people's expectations can create pressure. Even enjoyable activities become stressful if someone feels they must perform perfectly. Students, for example, may worry about several tasks at once. Having clear priorities and someone to discuss the problem with can make the workload feel more manageable.

items.question: Will you continue doing something when you are aware that it’s a waste of time?
items.questionZh: 明知浪费时间，你还会继续做某事吗？
items.answer: Sometimes, yes. It's easy to recognise that scrolling is taking too long and still keep doing it because the next video looks interesting. I'm trying to use a clear stopping point. items.question: How do you balance life and work?
items.questionZh: 你如何平衡生活与工作？
items.answer: As a student, I balance study and free time rather than a full-time job. I try to finish the most important task first and leave time for basketball or relaxing. A realistic plan helps more than filling every hour, because unexpected work and ordinary tiredness can change the day.

items.question: Is it good to have a daily routine?
items.questionZh: 有固定日常安排是好事吗？
items.answer: Yes, a simple routine reduces the number of small decisions people have to make. It can help them begin work without waiting to feel motivated. But the routine should allow some flexibility. If one unexpected event ruins the entire schedule, the plan is probably too strict to be useful.

items.question: Do you think stress is important in people's lives?
items.questionZh: 压力在人们生活中重要吗？
items.answer: A little pressure can make a deadline feel meaningful and encourage action. But I wouldn't describe constant stress as necessary for a good life. People also need rest and a sense that tasks are manageable. I'd prefer clear goals and steady effort to feeling under pressure all the time.
items.ideaZh: 适量压力可能推动行动，但长期压力不是好生活必需，应有休息和可实现的目标。

items.question: Do you think it is a good trend to have more big cities?
items.questionZh: 出现更多大城市是好趋势吗？
items.answer: It can bring opportunities if housing, transport and public services develop together. Larger cities may give people more choices for work and education. But growth alone isn't enough. If more residents arrive without suitable services, congestion and expensive housing can make daily life harder instead of improving it.

items.question: Do you think there are some people who enjoy crowded places?
items.questionZh: 有些人会喜欢拥挤的地方吗？
items.answer: Yes, some people enjoy the energy of a busy market, concert or shopping street. Being surrounded by others can make an event feel exciting. However, enjoying a crowd for an evening is different from wanting every daily journey to be crowded. Most people probably have limits depending on the situation.

items.question: Why do people go to crowded places?
items.questionZh: 人们为什么去拥挤的地方？
items.answer: Often because a place offers something they want, such as a popular restaurant or a special event. Sometimes crowds are unavoidable, as on public transport at busy times. So people aren't always choosing the crowd itself; they may simply accept it as part of getting somewhere or doing something enjoyable.
items.ideaZh: 通常为餐厅、活动或交通需求，未必喜欢人群本身，而是接受必要代价。

items.question: Will people use bikes more or less in cities in the future?
items.questionZh: 未来城市里骑自行车的人会更多还是更少？
items.answer: I think bicycle use could increase where cities provide safe routes and convenient parking. For short trips, cycling can be practical. But weather, distance and road safety will still matter. People are unlikely to cycle more just because they are encouraged to if the journey feels dangerous or uncomfortable.

items.question: Will there be more or less green space in cities in the future?
items.questionZh: 未来城市绿地会更多还是更少？
items.answer: That depends on planning choices. Growing cities may lose green space if every available area is built on, but they can also protect parks and include trees in new neighbourhoods. I'd hope for more useful green space close to homes, rather than only one large park far away.
items.ideaZh: 取决于规划，建设可能挤占绿地，也可保护并新增；更希望住宅附近有实用绿地。

items.question: Which cities are overcrowded in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家哪些城市过于拥挤？
items.answer: Large cities such as Beijing and Shanghai are places I'd associate with crowded transport at busy times. But I wouldn't call every neighbourhood overcrowded. A tourist street on a holiday can feel very different from the same city's quieter residential areas, so the time and location make a big difference.

items.question: Besides big historical events, what else is important when learning history?
items.questionZh: 学历史除了大事件，还有什么重要？
items.answer: Everyday life matters too: how people worked, learned, ate and raised families. Those details make history easier to connect with. It is also important to consider whose account we are reading. A major event can look different when described by a leader and by an ordinary person affected by it.

items.question: Do you think people should learn ancient history before learning modern history?
items.questionZh: 学近现代史前应该先学古代史吗？
items.answer: Learning in time order can help people understand connections, but I don't think it must always start with ancient history. A familiar modern event may first make someone interested. A teacher can then explain the earlier background. The main thing is giving learners a clear sense of when things happened.
items.ideaZh: 时间顺序有帮助但不必强制，熟悉的近代事件也能激发兴趣，再追溯背景。

items.question: Is it important to learn how people in the past lived their lives?
items.questionZh: 了解过去人们如何生活重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, because it helps explain how daily habits and institutions developed. It can also make us question things we now take for granted. Learning how ordinary families lived gives history a human side, instead of making the past seem like a list of rulers, dates and battles.
items.ideaZh: 帮助理解习惯制度的形成，也反思习以为常之事，让历史有人情而非只有帝王战役。

items.question: How do children learn history before they attend school?
items.questionZh: 学龄前孩子如何了解历史？
items.answer: They can hear family stories, look at old photographs and visit places with adults. At that age, simple questions work well, such as how grandparents travelled to school. Adults should explain which parts are remembered facts and which are stories, without overwhelming children with complicated dates.

items.question: At what age do you think people should begin to learn history?
items.questionZh: 应该从几岁开始学历史？
items.answer: They can begin quite young through simple stories about family and local places. Formal study can become more detailed once they can understand time and compare accounts. I wouldn't choose one exact age for everyone. The approach matters more than starting early just to memorise names and dates.

items.question: Do you think children should begin learning history from an early age?
items.questionZh: 孩子应该从小开始学历史吗？
items.answer: Yes, if it is presented in a way they can enjoy and understand. Old objects, pictures and family memories can make them curious about change. The aim should be interest and basic understanding. A long list of facts to memorise might make history feel difficult before they have a reason to care.

items.question: Why is self-discipline important when learning a new skill?
items.questionZh: 学新技能时自律为什么重要？
items.answer: A new skill usually improves through repeated practice, including days when progress feels slow. Self-discipline helps someone continue after the first excitement fades. Still, the plan needs to be realistic. A short practice session that happens regularly is more useful than an ambitious schedule that is abandoned after two days.
items.ideaZh: 进步要长期重复练习，自律帮助热情消退后继续，但短而规律比夸大计划有效。

items.question: What are the differences between learning from a teacher and learning by oneself?
items.questionZh: 跟老师学和自学有什么区别？
items.answer: A teacher can notice mistakes and suggest what to practise next. Learning alone gives someone more control over the pace and may cost less. I'd use both if possible. Independent practice builds experience, while occasional guidance can stop a learner from repeating the same problem without noticing it.
items.ideaZh: 老师能纠错指导，自学可控节奏省费用；最好独练与偶尔指导结合。

items.question: How do adults learn a new skill?
items.questionZh: 成年人如何学新技能？
items.answer: Many begin with a clear purpose, such as a task at work or a personal interest. They may use a course, online lessons or help from someone experienced. Since time is limited, practical exercises are useful. Applying a small new idea immediately can make it easier to understand and remember.
items.ideaZh: 常从工作或兴趣目的出发，用课程、网络或熟人帮助，及时实践小知识便于记忆。

items.question: How can parents and teachers teach children new skills?
items.questionZh: 家长和老师怎样教孩子新技能？
items.answer: They can demonstrate a small step, let the child try and give specific encouragement. Saying what improved is more helpful than simply saying good job every time. Tasks should become harder gradually, and adults should allow mistakes, so children feel comfortable practising rather than afraid of getting something wrong.

items.question: Where can children learn new skills?
items.questionZh: 孩子在哪里能学新技能？
items.answer: At school, at home and through clubs or activities with friends. Different places offer different opportunities: a classroom may teach a method, while a playground lets children try it socially. Online resources can help too, as long as the content suits their age and an adult gives support when needed.

items.question: Why should children learn new skills?
items.questionZh: 孩子为什么应该学新技能？
items.answer: New skills help children become more independent and discover what they enjoy. They also learn that improvement takes practice. Even if a child doesn't continue a particular hobby, finishing a small task or solving a problem can give them confidence to try something unfamiliar later.
items.ideaZh: 有助独立、发现兴趣并理解练习带来进步，即使不长期坚持该爱好也能积累自信。

items.question: Do people’s movie preferences change as they get older?
items.questionZh: 电影喜好会随年龄增长而变化吗？
items.answer: They can, because people's experiences and interests change. A film someone found boring as a child may become meaningful later. However, old favourites can remain enjoyable too. I think people often add new interests rather than completely stop liking the kinds of films they grew up with.
items.ideaZh: 可能随经历兴趣改变，也会保留旧爱好，常是增加新兴趣而非完全推翻过去。

items.question: Should documentary films be completely truthful?
items.questionZh: 纪录片应该完全真实吗？
items.answer: They should be accurate about the facts they present. Filmmakers still choose what to include, so no documentary can show every detail. If a scene is recreated or a point is uncertain, that should be clear. Viewers need to understand the difference between evidence and the filmmaker's interpretation.

items.question: Can movies help people better understand the cultural background of a country?
items.questionZh: 电影能帮助了解一个国家的文化背景吗？
items.answer: Yes, films can introduce daily habits, language and social issues in a memorable way. But one story can't represent a whole country. A viewer should avoid assuming that every person lives like the characters. Films are a useful starting point for curiosity, especially when followed by other sources or conversations.
items.ideaZh: 能展示习惯、语言和社会问题，但一部片不能代表全国，应结合其他资料。

items.question: Are movies more likely to help people become more creative than books?
items.questionZh: 电影比书更能培养创造力吗？
items.answer: Not necessarily. Films provide images, sound and examples of visual storytelling, which can inspire ideas. Books leave more of the scene for the reader to imagine. Both can support creativity; what matters is whether people think about what they experience and use it to create something of their own.
items.ideaZh: 不一定，电影提供视听示范，书留想象空间，关键是看后如何思考和创造。

items.question: What are the differences between watching movies at home and in a cinema?

items.answer: At home, people can choose the time, pause the film and spend less. A cinema offers a larger screen and a shared atmosphere, and there are usually fewer household distractions. I'd choose according to the film and the company. A family comedy can be just as enjoyable at home.

items.question: What kinds of movies are the most popular in China?

items.answer: I can't give an exact ranking, but comedies and action films seem popular among people I know. A familiar actor or an interesting story can attract viewers across different genres. Preferences vary, so a film that works well for a family outing may not be someone's first choice when watching alone.

items.question: What problems does it cause for transportation when everyone commutes at the same time?
items.questionZh: 所有人同时通勤会给交通带来什么问题？
items.answer: It creates a sharp rise in demand over a short period. Roads become congested, while buses and trains may be crowded even if they have spare capacity later. Journeys become less predictable too. Flexible starting times could help some workers, alongside reliable public transport and safer options for short trips.

items.question: What are the benefits of travelling abroad?
items.questionZh: 出国旅行有什么好处？
items.answer: People can experience different daily routines, try unfamiliar food and practise communicating outside their usual environment. It may also challenge assumptions about another place. The benefit depends on how someone travels, though. Paying attention and talking respectfully with people can teach more than rushing through a list of sights.

items.question: Which is better for knowing more about a country? Travelling or reading books about it?
items.questionZh: 了解国家时，旅行与读相关书籍哪个更好？
items.answer: They offer different kinds of understanding. Books can explain history and wider patterns, while travel gives direct experience of particular places and people. I'd combine them. A short visit alone may create a narrow impression, and reading beforehand can help a traveller understand what they are seeing.

items.question: How much time do you think people should spend on a trip abroad?
items.questionZh: 出国旅行应该花多长时间？
items.answer: It depends on distance, purpose and budget. For a nearby destination, a week may allow a relaxed visit, while a long journey might justify more time. I think leaving room to rest and explore matters more than reaching a fixed number of days or visiting as many places as possible.

items.question: Who prefers travelling abroad? The young or the old?

items.answer: Either group may enjoy it. Younger people might be attracted by new experiences, while some older people have more time after retirement. items.question: Do Chinese people like travelling abroad?
items.questionZh: 中国人喜欢出国旅行吗？
items.answer: Some do, because they want to experience a different culture or scenery. Others prefer travelling within China for reasons such as cost, language or convenience. Among any large population, preferences vary. A person may also choose differently depending on how much time they have and who they are travelling with.

items.question: Why do people want to be popular?

items.answer: People often want to feel accepted and included. Being popular may bring more chances to join activities or have their ideas heard. But trying to please everyone can become tiring. I think a few reliable friendships can be more valuable than getting attention from a large number of people.

items.question: Is it easier to become popular nowadays?

items.answer: It may be easier to reach a large audience online, because a short video can be shared quickly. But attention can disappear just as quickly, and many people are competing for it. Becoming briefly well known is different from building lasting respect or close relationships.

items.question: What are the qualities of being a good teacher?
items.questionZh: 好老师应该具备什么品质？
items.answer: A good teacher needs clear explanations, patience and a fair attitude. Knowing the subject is essential, but they also need to notice when students haven't understood. Useful feedback matters too. A teacher who helps learners see what to improve can build confidence without pretending that every answer is already perfect.

items.question: Do you think good teachers are always popular among students?
items.questionZh: 好老师总是受学生欢迎吗？
items.answer: Not always. A teacher may set challenging work or enforce rules that students don't enjoy at the time. If the approach is fair and helpful, students may appreciate it later. Being entertaining can help with attention, but popularity alone doesn't show whether someone teaches effectively.

items.question: Is it important for a teacher to be popular?
items.questionZh: 老师受欢迎重要吗？
items.answer: A positive relationship helps students feel comfortable asking questions, so being approachable matters. However, popularity shouldn't be the main goal. Teachers sometimes need to make unpopular decisions. I'd value respect and trust more than simply being liked because lessons are easy or there is very little homework.
items.ideaZh: 亲切可接近有利于提问，但不应追求讨好，尊重信任比轻松少作业更重要。

items.question: Why are some students popular in school?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些学生在学校受欢迎？
items.answer: Some are friendly, funny or good at bringing people into a group. Others become known through sport or school activities. I think kindness helps popularity last: classmates are more likely to enjoy being with someone who listens and includes them than someone who only wants attention.

items.question: Why are there so few top athletes?
items.questionZh: 为什么顶尖运动员这么少？
items.answer: Reaching the top requires an unusual combination of ability, long-term training and opportunities. Many people work hard, but competition becomes extremely strong at that level. Support, good coaching and staying able to compete matter too. So effort is essential, but it doesn't guarantee that everyone can become a champion.

items.answer: I'd hesitate to name just one. Basketball is very visible around my school, and table tennis is another sport people commonly associate with China. The answer may also change depending on whether we mean playing or watching. My own interest in basketball probably makes me notice it more.

items.question: Is it easy to identify children’s talents?
items.questionZh: 识别孩子的天赋容易吗？
items.answer: Not always, because children develop at different speeds and may not have tried the activity that suits them. Early success can be a clue, but it isn't a complete prediction. Giving children varied opportunities and watching their interest over time seems fairer than labelling them as talented or untalented too quickly.

items.question: Is talent important in sports?
items.questionZh: 运动中天赋重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, natural ability can be an advantage, especially in very competitive sport. But technique, practice and teamwork still matter. Someone who learns quickly may stop improving if they avoid effort. For ordinary people, enjoying an activity and taking part regularly can be valuable even without exceptional talent.

items.question: What qualities should an athlete have?
items.questionZh: 运动员应具备哪些品质？
items.answer: An athlete needs discipline, patience and the ability to respond to setbacks. In team sports, listening and cooperating are important too. Losing a match or making a mistake shouldn't mean giving up. Being willing to review what happened and practise a specific weakness helps turn effort into improvement.
items.ideaZh: 自律、耐心、应对挫折和合作能力，愿意复盘并练具体弱点才能进步。

items.question: Should students have physical education and do sports at school?

The aim should include enjoyment, movement and teamwork, rather than only finding the fastest or most competitive pupils.

items.question: Is it better to live in an apartment than in a house?
items.questionZh: 住公寓比住独栋房屋好吗？
items.answer: It depends on the person's needs. An apartment may be easier to maintain and closer to useful services, while a house can offer more space and privacy. Cost and travel time matter too. I would choose a home that suits daily life rather than assume one type is always better.

items.question: Do you think all old buildings should be demolished?
items.questionZh: 所有旧建筑都应该拆除吗？
items.answer: No, age alone isn't a good reason to demolish a building. Some old buildings have historical value or can still serve a useful purpose after repairs. Others may be unsafe or unsuitable. Each case needs careful assessment, including whether improvement is possible and what the local community would lose.

items.question: Do you think old buildings are valuable?
items.questionZh: 你觉得旧建筑有价值吗？
items.answer: Many are valuable because they show how a place developed and connect people with its past. Some also have distinctive design or personal meaning for residents. That doesn't mean every old structure must stay unchanged. The challenge is preserving what matters while allowing buildings to remain safe and useful.

items.question: What special events are celebrated in your country?

items.answer: People celebrate festivals such as Chinese New Year, as well as personal occasions like birthdays, weddings and graduations. Different events bring different groups together. items.answer: It depends on the size and purpose of the party. A private home feels personal and gives people more control, but preparation and cleaning take work. A public venue may be easier for a large group. I'd think about the guests' comfort and the practical effort before choosing.

items.answer: People often hold parties to mark a birthday, achievement or major life change. They also need a time when guests are available, so weekends can be convenient. items.question: What effect does stress have on health?
items.questionZh: 压力对健康有什么影响？
items.answer: Stress can affect sleep and concentration, and it may make someone feel tense or tired. The effect differs from person to person. A short busy period is different from feeling overwhelmed for a long time. I think recognising the pressure and getting appropriate support is more helpful than pretending it isn't there.

items.question: Which group pays more attention to health, young people or old people?
items.questionZh: 年轻人和老人哪一群更关注健康？
items.answer: Older people may pay more attention when they have health concerns, while some young people focus on fitness or sport. But age isn't the only factor. items.question: Are success books useful to everyone?
items.questionZh: 成功学书籍对所有人都有用吗？
items.answer: No single book is useful to everyone. Advice that fits a business owner may not suit a student with different resources. Some success books offer useful habits, but readers should question big promises. I'd look for ideas I can apply sensibly rather than assume copying a successful person's routine guarantees the same result.

items.question: Do you think people should read the original book before watching the movie?

items.answer: They don't have to. Reading first can give more detail and leave room to imagine the characters, while a film may make someone interested in the book. I'd treat them as different versions of a story. Enjoying one doesn't require following a fixed order or judging every difference as a mistake.

items.question: What kinds of books are popular in China?

items.answer: I'm not sure about national rankings, but people around me read novels, study materials and books related to personal interests. items.question: Should children be taught to be kind to others?
items.questionZh: 应该教育孩子善待别人吗？
items.answer: Yes, and everyday examples are a good starting point. Children can learn to notice when someone needs help, take turns and speak respectfully. They also need to understand personal boundaries. Being kind shouldn't mean agreeing to everything; it means treating others with care while still being able to say no.

items.question: Should people be very kind when they help others?
items.questionZh: 帮助别人时应该很友善吗？
items.answer: Yes, the way help is offered matters. Someone may feel embarrassed about needing support, so listening and asking what would be useful can protect their dignity. Kindness doesn't need to be dramatic. A calm explanation or a small practical action may help more than giving advice the person never wanted.
items.ideaZh: 态度很重要，应先倾听需要，保护对方尊严，实际小帮助比强加建议好。

items.question: Can kids provide any help to parents?

items.answer: Certainly. Children can put away their belongings, help set the table or take responsibility for a simple household task. The activity should match their age and ability. Helping gives them a sense of contribution, but they shouldn't be expected to take on responsibilities that are too difficult or unsafe.

items.question: Should parents give children advice? Why?

items.answer: Yes, parents can offer experience and help children think through consequences. However, advice works better as a conversation than an order, especially as children become older. items.question: Are there any differences between the videos that young people and old people like to watch?

items.answer: There may be differences in topics because their interests and routines differ. Still, plenty of videos appeal across ages, and personal interests tell us more than age alone.

items.questionZh: 男性和女性喜欢的视频有什么不同？
items.answer: There may be patterns in particular groups, but I wouldn't use gender to predict an individual's taste. A young woman may love gaming videos, and a young man may enjoy cooking. Friends, hobbies and the suggestions a person sees online can all influence what they choose to watch.

items.question: What makes a video go viral online?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些视频会突然走红？
items.answer: A clear idea, strong emotion or something unexpected can make people want to share a video. Timing and who first shares it may matter too. However, popularity is hard to predict. A useful or funny video can spread quickly, but attention alone doesn't tell us whether its information is reliable.

items.question: Why do most children think education is boring?
items.questionZh: 为什么大多数孩子觉得上学很无聊？
items.answer: I wouldn't assume most children find all education boring. They may lose interest when tasks are repetitive, too difficult or disconnected from anything they understand. Giving a clear purpose and letting them participate can help. Even a familiar subject can feel different when children get to test an idea themselves.

items.question: Why aren’t young people willing to listen to the experiences of older people?
items.questionZh: 为什么年轻人不愿听年长者分享经验？
items.answer: Sometimes the advice feels unrelated to their current situation, or it is delivered as a lecture. That can make young people stop listening even when the experience is valuable. A specific story and a genuine conversation usually work better than assuming the younger person must accept every conclusion.

items.question: What can people do when they feel bored?
items.questionZh: 人们觉得无聊时可以做什么？
items.answer: A small change of activity can help, such as taking a walk, calling a friend or trying a manageable task. It is also worth asking why they feel bored. Someone who needs rest may not benefit from another demanding activity, while someone who lacks challenge may enjoy learning a new skill.
items.ideaZh: 可以散步、联系朋友或完成一个小任务；先分清自己需要休息还是需要新的挑战。

items.question: Why are some teachers’ classes boring? Are there any solutions?
items.questionZh: 老师的课让学生觉得无聊时，应该怎么办？
items.answer: A lesson may rely too heavily on one-way explanation, or the pace may not match the students. Teachers could break the material into shorter sections and include questions or practical examples. They also need feedback from learners, because silence doesn't always mean everyone has understood or is interested.
items.ideaZh: 减少长时间单向讲解，分段加入提问和实际例子，并听取学生反馈、调整节奏。

items.question: Why do some young people feel bored when talking with old people?
items.questionZh: 为什么年轻人与老年人聊天时会觉得无聊？
items.answer: They may have different interests, or the conversation may repeat stories without inviting the younger person to join in. But this isn't unavoidable. Finding a shared topic, such as sport, food or family memories, can make the conversation enjoyable. How people listen matters as much as their ages.

items.question: Do most people think news about celebrities is boring?

items.answer: No, reactions vary. Some people enjoy following a favourite actor or athlete, while others find the topic unimportant. I think the quality of the story matters: an interview about someone's work offers more than a headline designed only to attract attention.

items.question: Do you know anyone who likes to get up early?
items.questionZh: 你认识早起的人吗？
items.answer: My grandfather is the example I'd give. He likes a quiet start and spends some time looking after his plants before the day gets busy. That routine suits him. It also shows that getting up early can be enjoyable when people have a reason, rather than simply being forced to rush.

items.question: Why do people get up early?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人喜欢早起？
items.answer: Some need to travel to work or school, while others want quiet time for exercise or household tasks. An early start can make the morning less rushed. But the benefit depends on their overall routine; getting up early is not automatically useful if they have stayed awake too late.
items.ideaZh: 有人要上班上学，有人享受安静地运动或做事；前提是睡眠充足，不能认为早起必然更好。

items.question: What kinds of occasions need people to arrive early?
items.questionZh: 什么场合需要提前到达？
items.answer: Flights, important exams and job interviews usually require some extra time. Arriving before the required time allows people to find the right place and handle small delays. The amount should be reasonable, though. It is better to check the instructions than assume every event needs the same preparation.

items.question: Why do some people like to stay up late?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人喜欢熬夜？
items.answer: Some enjoy the quiet after daily responsibilities are finished. Others become absorbed in games, films or conversations and lose track of time. Work schedules can be another reason.
