items.question: Is it good to arrive early in any situation?
items.questionZh: 所有场合提前到都好吗？

items.question: What are the advantages of growing vegetables or flowers at home?

items.question: Do you think students should learn to grow plant?

items.answer: Yes, a small project can teach patience and observation. Students can see that living things need consistent care, rather than an instant result. items.question: What rules should students follow at school?
items.questionZh: 学校通常有哪些规则？
items.answer: Students should respect others, arrive on time and follow safety rules. They also need clear expectations about schoolwork and shared spaces. The rules should have a sensible purpose. Explaining how quiet behaviour helps people concentrate, for example, is more useful than expecting children to obey without understanding anything.

items.question: Do people in your country usually obey the law?
items.questionZh: 你们国家的人遵守法律吗？
items.answer: In ordinary life, I see people generally trying to follow rules, but I can't make a reliable claim about the whole country. Behaviour also depends on understanding and enforcement. Clear information and fair treatment can encourage cooperation more effectively than leaving people confused about what is expected.

items.question: What kinds of behavior are considered as good behavior?
items.questionZh: 什么是良好的行为？
items.answer: Treating others respectfully, keeping promises and taking responsibility for mistakes are good examples. Context matters as well: good behaviour in a library includes being quiet, while in a team it includes participating. items.question: Do you think children can learn about the law outside of school?
items.questionZh: 孩子除了在学校，还能在哪里了解法律？
items.answer: Yes, through family conversations, public information and everyday situations. A parent can explain why people wait at a road crossing or respect someone else's belongings. items.question: What are the benefits for people to obey rules?
items.questionZh: 遵守规则有什么好处？
items.answer: Reasonable rules make shared situations more predictable. People can travel, study or work with less confusion because they know what to expect from others. Following a queue is a simple example. The benefits are strongest when the rules apply fairly, rather than giving some people special treatment without a good reason.

items.question: How can parents teach children to obey rules?
items.questionZh: 父母应该怎样教孩子守规则？
items.answer: Parents should explain the reason, model the behaviour and apply expectations consistently. A child is unlikely to take a rule seriously if adults ignore it whenever it is inconvenient. It also helps to praise specific responsible behaviour and give children a chance to ask questions about rules they don't understand.

items.questionZh: 你还和儿时的朋友保持联系吗？
items.answer: Yes, I still keep in touch with a few, including my friend Leo. Having shared memories makes conversation easy, even when we have been busy. We don't need to speak every day, but making occasional plans helps the friendship remain part of our current lives rather than only a memory.

items.question: How important is childhood friendship to children?
items.questionZh: 儿时的友谊为什么重要？
items.answer: It can give children a sense of belonging and a chance to learn cooperation. Friends practise sharing, handling disagreement and supporting each other in ordinary situations. items.question: What do you think of communicating via social media?
items.questionZh: 你怎么看社交媒体？
items.answer: It is useful for staying in touch across distance and arranging things quickly. However, short messages can be misunderstood because tone is less clear. items.question: Do you think online communication through social media will replace face-to-face communication?
items.questionZh: 社交媒体可以取代面对面交流吗？
items.answer: I don't think it will replace it completely. Online contact is convenient, but spending time together gives people shared experiences and makes expressions easier to read. items.question: What's the difference between having younger friends and older friends?
items.questionZh: 年轻人和老年人可以成为朋友吗？
items.answer: Older friends may offer experience of situations you haven't reached yet, while younger friends may introduce different interests or perspectives. But those are possibilities, not fixed roles. A good friendship still depends on respect and shared enjoyment, rather than one person always being the adviser because of their age.
items.ideaZh: 可以交流经验和新视角，但不必固定成一方指导另一方；尊重和相处愉快才是基础。

items.question: Has technology changed people's friendships? How?
items.questionZh: 科技如何改变了交朋友的方式？
items.answer: Yes, it makes keeping in touch easier when people move away, and shared online interests can help new friendships begin. At the same time, constant contact doesn't always mean a close relationship. Friends still need attention and genuine conversation, whether they communicate through a screen or meet in person.
items.ideaZh: 跨距离联系和认识新人更容易，但消息多不等于亲密；仍需要认真关注和真实交流。

items.question: Do you think being a doctor is easy or difficult?
items.questionZh: 当医生容易还是困难？
items.answer: I think it is difficult because it requires a great deal of learning and responsibility. Doctors need to understand complex information and communicate clearly with people who may be worried. The work can also involve uncertainty. Knowing facts is important, but making careful decisions and explaining them is a challenge too.
items.ideaZh: 需要长期学习并承担责任，处理复杂信息，还要向担忧的患者清楚解释不确定情况。

items.question: Do you think learning biology is interesting for children?
items.questionZh: 孩子会觉得生物学有趣吗？
items.answer: It can be, especially when it connects with things children can observe, such as plants, animals or their own senses. A simple activity may raise questions more effectively than a long definition. Teachers need to match the detail to the age group so curiosity isn't lost in difficult language.
items.ideaZh: 植物、动物和人体感官都能观察；适龄活动通常比只背定义更能激发兴趣。

items.question: Why do some children want to become doctors?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些孩子想当医生？
items.answer: Some want to help people, while others have been influenced by a doctor who cared for someone in their family. They may also find the human body interesting. As they get older, learning more about the training and daily work can help them decide whether the career really suits them.
items.ideaZh: 想帮助别人、受家人或医生影响，或对人体感兴趣；做决定前应了解训练和实际工作。

items.question: Do you think governments should put a large amount of money into medical research?
items.questionZh: 政府应该资助医学研究吗？
items.answer: Yes, I think medical research deserves strong public support because useful discoveries can benefit many people. Funding should still be carefully managed and priorities explained. Governments also need to support everyday services, so the question isn't research or care, but how to balance future improvements with current needs.
items.ideaZh: 研究能使公众受益，但应明确优先事项、透明管理，同时平衡眼前医疗需求和未来进步。

items.question: Why is some doctors’ pay high and others’ low?
items.questionZh: 为什么医生之间的收入有差距？
items.answer: Pay can vary with experience, responsibilities, working location and the organisation employing them. A role requiring rare specialist skills may be paid differently from an entry-level position. I don't think salary always reflects effort fairly, though. Workload and the value of basic community care should also be considered.
items.ideaZh: 经验、地区、责任、雇主及稀缺技能都可能影响收入；收入不一定完全反映付出与价值。

items.question: Do you think doctors should be paid more?
items.questionZh: 医生应该获得更高收入吗？
items.answer: Where pay is low compared with responsibility and workload, an increase could be justified. But better working conditions and enough staff matter too. I would look at the particular roles rather than make one rule for every doctor. Fair pay should help services keep capable people without ignoring other healthcare workers.
items.ideaZh: 如果收入与负担不匹配，可以提高；也应改善人手和工作条件，并考虑其他医疗工作者。

items.question: Why do some people start their own business?
items.questionZh: 为什么人们想自己创业？
items.answer: Some want more control over their work, while others see a problem they think they can solve. They may also want to turn an interest into an income. However, running a business involves uncertainty and responsibility, so independence doesn't necessarily mean an easier life or fewer working hours.
items.ideaZh: 希望有自主权、解决问题或把兴趣变成收入；同时也要承担不确定性和更多责任。

items.question: Should governments provide financial support to start-ups?
items.questionZh: 政府应该给创业者资金支持吗？
items.answer: Some support can be useful, especially when an idea offers a clear public benefit or helps people develop valuable skills. But support needs clear conditions and review. Advice, training or access to shared facilities may help as well. Simply giving money without checking the plan could waste limited resources.
items.ideaZh: 可支持有公共价值或培养技能的项目，但要有明确条件和检查；培训及共享设施也是帮助。

items.question: Do most people prefer shopping at big stores or small stores?
items.questionZh: 大多数人更喜欢大商店还是小商店？
items.answer: I don't know which most people prefer overall. Big stores offer variety and convenient comparison, while small shops may provide personal service or be closer to home. People can use both for different purchases. The type of product and the quality of the particular shop often determine the choice.
items.ideaZh: 不假定大多数人的选择；大店方便比较、品类多，小店可能更近、服务更个人化，取决于购买需求。

items.question: What makes a business successful?
items.questionZh: 企业成功需要什么？
items.answer: It needs to solve a real customer problem at a price that covers its costs. Reliable service and listening to feedback help keep people coming back. A small restaurant, for example, doesn't need a huge menu if customers trust the food and feel welcome whenever they visit.
items.ideaZh: 解决真实需求、控制成本、可靠服务并听取反馈；小餐馆赢得信任比菜单特别大更重要。

items.question: What makes a business fail?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些企业会失败？
items.answer: A business may fail if it spends more than it can support, misunderstands customers or loses their trust. Poor communication within the team can make problems worse. Sometimes outside conditions change too. So failure isn't always caused by laziness; a workable idea still needs careful management and some flexibility.
items.ideaZh: 可能支出过高、不懂顾客、失去信任或沟通不畅，也可能遭遇外部变化，不能只归因于不努力。

items.question: Is it easy to set up a new business in your country?
items.questionZh: 在你们国家创业容易吗？
items.answer: I wouldn't call it easy just because a small business can begin online or from a modest space. Owners still need to understand the relevant requirements, find customers and manage costs. I haven't started one myself, but I think maintaining a steady business is a bigger challenge than simply getting started.
items.ideaZh: 小型线上业务可能较容易开始，但还要处理要求、成本和客户问题；没有亲身创业经验，持续经营比开张难。

items.question: Do people often change their plans?
items.questionZh: 人们经常改变计划吗？
items.answer: Yes, because plans depend on information that can change. Weather, transport or another person's availability may require an adjustment. Changing a plan isn't necessarily a sign of poor organisation. A useful plan gives direction while leaving room to respond sensibly when circumstances are different from what someone expected.
items.ideaZh: 天气、交通或参与者时间改变时需要调整；这不一定是安排不好，灵活性也很重要。

items.question: Would you tell others if you change your plan?
items.questionZh: 改变计划时应该告诉别人吗？
items.answer: Yes, if the change affects them. I'd explain it as soon as I could, especially if they had arranged their time around the original plan. A short clear message is usually enough. Waiting until the last minute can cause more inconvenience than the change itself.
items.ideaZh: 如果影响别人，应尽早清楚通知，尊重对方安排，避免最后一刻才说。

items.question: Why do you think parents still make plans for their children nowadays?
items.questionZh: 父母为什么喜欢为孩子做计划？
items.answer: They want to protect their children and may believe their experience helps them see future consequences. Younger children do need guidance. As children grow, though, involving them in the plan becomes more important. Otherwise, the parents may create a schedule that fits their own expectations more than the child's needs.
items.ideaZh: 想保护孩子，也相信自己的经验；年幼时需要指导，长大后应更多参与决定，避免只服从父母期待。

items.question: How does technology help people make plans?
items.questionZh: 科技如何帮助人们做计划？
items.answer: Calendars and reminders help people remember tasks, while maps and weather information can help with travel plans. Shared tools make group arrangements easier too. However, technology can't choose priorities for us. Putting too many tasks into an app doesn't make an unrealistic schedule possible to follow.
items.ideaZh: 日历、提醒、地图、天气和共享工具都方便，但工具不能替人选择重点或让不切实际的安排变合理。

items.question: What kind of plans do people often make?
items.questionZh: 人们通常会做哪些计划？
items.answer: People make plans for daily tasks, study, trips and larger goals such as changing jobs. The amount of detail depends on the purpose. Planning an ordinary afternoon may take a short list, while arranging a group trip requires discussion of dates, cost and what everyone wants to do.

items.question: Do you think people like the process of making plans more, or the moment of carrying them out?
items.questionZh: 人们更喜欢制订计划还是执行计划？
items.answer: It varies. Planning can be enjoyable because people imagine a good result without facing the effort yet. Carrying out a plan can be more satisfying because it produces something real. I think the best feeling often comes when a manageable plan leads to visible progress, even if some details change.

items.question: Why do some people prefer to work by themselves?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人更喜欢独立工作？
items.answer: They may concentrate better alone or prefer controlling the pace and method. Independent work also avoids delays caused by coordinating with others. However, working alone limits access to feedback. I think the choice should depend on the task, rather than assuming teamwork or independence is always the better approach.

items.question: What should a leader do to make team members want to follow him or her?
items.questionZh: 领导怎样才能让团队成员愿意跟随？
items.answer: A leader should explain the goal, listen and treat people fairly. Following through on promises builds trust. Team members are more willing to cooperate when they understand why their work matters and see that the leader accepts responsibility too, rather than only giving orders when things are going badly.
items.ideaZh: 讲清目标、公平倾听并兑现承诺；成员看到领导也承担责任，才更愿意合作。

items.question: Should students learn to do group work?
items.questionZh: 学生应该学习小组合作吗？
items.answer: Yes, because many real tasks require people to share ideas and responsibilities. Students need practice discussing disagreements and keeping others informed. Teachers should make each person's role reasonably clear, though. Otherwise, a group task can become one person doing the work while everyone receives the same credit.

items.question: What group tasks are there in schools?
items.questionZh: 学校里有哪些小组任务？
items.answer: Schools use group presentations, science projects, performances and team sports. In computer courses, students might build a small website together. Each task develops slightly different skills, but they all require some coordination. It helps when the work genuinely benefits from cooperation rather than simply putting several names on one answer.
items.ideaZh: 展示、科学项目、演出和团队运动都很常见，计算机课还可合作建网站；任务应真正需要合作。

items.question: What advantages are there for students experiencing teamwork at school?
items.questionZh: 在学校体验团队合作有什么好处？
items.answer: They can learn to explain ideas, divide work and respond to feedback. They also see that classmates may approach the same problem differently. Those experiences are useful beyond a single subject. A successful group project teaches students that reliability and communication can matter alongside individual academic ability.
items.ideaZh: 练习解释、分工和回应反馈，认识不同解题方式；可靠性和沟通能力也很重要。

items.question: How can you tell if a person is a good leader?
items.questionZh: 怎样判断一个人是不是好领导？
items.answer: I'd look at whether the group understands its goals and whether members feel able to contribute. A good leader helps people solve problems and takes responsibility when decisions don't work. Being the loudest person isn't enough. The team's behaviour often tells us more than the leader's description of themselves.
items.ideaZh: 看团队是否清楚目标、成员能否贡献，以及领导是否帮助解决问题并担责；声音最大并不等于领导力强。

items.question: Do you think children sometimes have to make important decisions?
items.questionZh: 孩子有时也需要作重要决定吗？
items.answer: Yes, although adults should support choices with serious consequences. A child may need to decide how to respond to a friendship problem or which activity to commit to. Giving suitable choices helps them practise judgment. They shouldn't have to carry responsibility for major adult problems they cannot control.

items.question: What important decisions do teenagers need to make after graduation?
items.questionZh: 青少年毕业后要作哪些重要决定？
items.answer: They may need to choose further study, a training course or a first job. Some also decide whether to move away from home. These choices involve interests, costs and available opportunities. Good guidance helps, but teenagers should be able to explain their own priorities instead of simply following what friends choose.

items.question: Who can children turn to for help when making a decision?
items.questionZh: 孩子作决定时可以向谁求助？
items.answer: Parents, teachers and other trusted adults can help them think through options. Friends may understand the immediate situation, but they may not have enough experience for every problem. The best person depends on the question. A teacher may explain a course more clearly, while family can discuss practical support.
items.ideaZh: 父母、老师及可信赖的成人；朋友了解眼前处境，但经验有限，应按问题选择合适的人。

items.question: Do you think advertisements can influence our decisions when shopping?
items.questionZh: 广告会影响购物决定吗？
items.answer: Yes, advertisements can make a product familiar or connect it with a feeling we want. That may influence which options we notice first, even if we don't buy immediately. Comparing actual features and price helps. An attractive image can introduce an item, but it shouldn't be the only reason for choosing it.

items.question: Do you think the influence of advertising is good?
items.questionZh: 广告的影响是好的吗？
items.answer: It can be useful when advertising explains a genuine benefit and helps people compare options. It becomes less helpful when it exaggerates results or creates pressure to buy unnecessary things. I'd judge the information and how it is presented, rather than call all advertising influence either good or bad.
items.ideaZh: 真实介绍产品、帮助比较时有益；夸大效果或诱导不必要消费时有害，应具体判断信息与表达方式。

items.question: How do people usually make important decisions?
items.questionZh: 人们通常怎样作重要决定？
items.answer: They often gather information, consider the likely results and discuss the options with people they trust. Personal values still matter, because two reasonable people can want different outcomes. For a major choice, I'd also think about whether it can be changed later and what support would be available if problems arose.
items.ideaZh: 收集信息、考虑后果、向可信的人讨论，同时结合个人价值观；重大选择还要考虑能否调整及遇事可获得的支持。
items.vocab: outcomes — 结果；personal values — 个人价值观

items.question: Why do some people like to watch sports events?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人喜欢看体育比赛？
items.answer: They enjoy the uncertainty, skill and shared excitement. Supporting a team can also give friends something to talk about. People who play the sport may notice techniques they want to learn, while other viewers simply enjoy the atmosphere. The appeal doesn't depend on being an expert in every rule.
items.ideaZh: 享受悬念、技术和共同的兴奋，也能与朋友讨论或学习动作；不必精通所有规则才能喜欢。
items.vocab: uncertainty — 结果的不确定性；atmosphere — 气氛

items.question: Where do people normally watch sports events?
items.questionZh: 人们通常在哪里看体育比赛？
items.answer: Many watch at home on a television or online, while others go to a sports ground or watch with friends in a public venue. The choice depends on time, cost and availability. A local school match is much easier to attend than a major event in another city.
items.ideaZh: 家里看电视或网络直播，也会去场馆或公共场所与朋友观看；取决于时间、费用和可达性。

items.question: What are the advantages of watching sports events online?
items.questionZh: 在网上看体育比赛有什么好处？
items.answer: It saves travel time and can make events accessible to people who live far away. Depending on the service, viewers may also be able to review key moments. However, the quality depends on the connection and coverage. It is convenient, but it doesn't fully reproduce the atmosphere of being there.
items.ideaZh: 节省路程，远方观众也能看，有些服务可回放精彩片段；但受网络和转播影响，难完全代替现场气氛。

items.question: What sports matches are suitable for children to attend?
items.questionZh: 哪些体育比赛适合带孩子去看？
items.answer: Local or school matches can be suitable because they are often shorter and easier to understand. The venue should be safe, and adults should consider noise, crowds and the child's interest. An expensive ticket doesn't guarantee a good experience if the child is tired or doesn't enjoy the sport.
items.ideaZh: 当地或学校比赛通常较短、较好理解；还要看安全、噪声、人群和兴趣，贵票不保证好体验。

items.question: Why do some people spend a lot going to other countries to watch sports events?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人花很多钱出国看比赛？
items.answer: For a dedicated fan, seeing a major event in person may be a rare experience connected with a favourite team or athlete. They might combine it with a holiday. Whether the cost is worthwhile is personal, but it makes sense that something with strong emotional meaning can become a travel priority.
items.ideaZh: 忠实球迷把亲眼看偶像或大赛当成难得经历，也可结合旅行；强烈情感让它成为个人优先事项。
items.vocab: dedicated fan — 忠实球迷；worthwhile — 值得的

items.question: What sports games are popular in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家哪些体育运动或比赛受欢迎？
items.answer: Basketball and table tennis are examples that come to mind. Around my school, basketball is especially noticeable because students can play together after class. Other people enjoy football, badminton or different activities. I'd distinguish between sports people regularly play and events that attract large audiences on television.

items.question: Why are there special foods on special occasions or events?
items.questionZh: 为什么特殊场合会有特别的食物？
items.answer: Special food helps people recognise an occasion and connect it with shared memories. Preparing and eating it together can become part of the celebration. The meaning may be more important than the cost. Birthday noodles, for example, can express a wish for a long life through a familiar family meal.
items.ideaZh: 食物标记节日、连接共同回忆，准备和分享也是庆祝的一部分；如长寿面表达祝愿，意义不在价格。

items.question: What are the differences between everyday food and festival food?
items.questionZh: 日常食物和节日食物有什么不同？
items.answer: Festival food may take more preparation or carry a symbolic meaning, while everyday meals are usually chosen for convenience and routine needs. But the difference isn't always in the ingredients. A simple dish can feel special when someone prepares it for a birthday and the family sits down to share it.
items.ideaZh: 节日食物可能更费工或有象征意义，日常饭菜更重方便；普通菜也可因生日和团聚变特别。

items.question: Are there any differences between the food people eat today and the food people ate in the past?
items.questionZh: 现在和过去人们吃的东西有什么不同？
items.answer: People in some places now have more choices and easier access to food from other regions. Ordering a prepared meal may also fit a busy schedule. Still, traditional home cooking remains important to many families. The differences depend on location and lifestyle, so there isn't one experience shared by everyone.
items.ideaZh: 部分地区选择更多、外地食物更容易获得，忙碌时也会点餐；家常传统饮食仍重要，差异取决于地区和生活方式。

items.question: Do people today prefer eating at home or in a restaurant?
items.questionZh: 现在人们更喜欢在家吃还是去餐馆？
items.answer: It depends on the occasion. Eating at home can be comfortable and give people control over the meal, while restaurants save cooking and cleaning time. A family may choose home on ordinary days and a restaurant for a larger gathering. I don't think one preference explains everyone's daily choices.
items.ideaZh: 看场合：在家舒适、能自己控制饭菜，餐馆省做饭清洗时间；普通日与大型聚会可作不同选择。

items.topic: 擅长学习和说语言的人
items.question: Are there many people who can speak foreign languages in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家会说外语的人多吗？
items.answer: Quite a few people I know have studied English, but their confidence in speaking varies. Knowing some vocabulary is different from holding a comfortable conversation. People who use a language regularly may have more practice, so I'd avoid judging ability only by whether someone studied it at school.
items.ideaZh: 身边不少人学过英语，但口语信心不同；认识单词不等于能自在交谈，应看实际使用情况。

items.question: Does speaking other languages help at work?
items.questionZh: 会其他语言对工作有帮助吗？
items.answer: It can help when someone communicates with overseas colleagues or needs information in another language. It may also make travel for work easier. But usefulness depends on the job. Language skills are most valuable when combined with the ability to do the work itself, rather than treated as a replacement for professional knowledge.

items.topic: 擅长学习和说语言的人
items.question: Do people learn any languages other than English?
items.questionZh: 人们会学习英语以外的语言吗？
items.answer: Yes, some people learn languages such as Japanese, Korean or French because of study, work or personal interests. A favourite film or music scene can be the starting point. The choice often feels more motivating when someone has a clear reason to use the language outside a lesson.

items.topic: 擅长学习和说语言的人
items.question: Why is it easier for children to learn new things than for adults?
items.questionZh: 为什么孩子学新东西比成人容易？
items.answer: It isn't always easier, but children may have more opportunities to practise and less fear of looking inexperienced. Adults can be busy and compare themselves with stronger learners. On the other hand, adults often have clear goals. I think suitable practice and encouragement make a difference at any age.

items.question: How do people learn new things?
items.questionZh: 人们如何学习新事物？
items.answer: They observe, listen, read and then try things themselves. Feedback helps them notice what needs improvement. For a practical skill, I think small tasks work well because the learner can see whether an idea works. Just collecting information may feel productive without actually building the ability to use it.

items.topic: 擅长学习和说语言的人
items.question: What is the most important thing for learning a language well?
items.questionZh: 学好一门语言最重要的是什么？
items.answer: Regular use is very important. People need chances to express real ideas, listen and notice gaps in their understanding. Accuracy matters, but waiting until every sentence is perfect can prevent practice. I'd combine manageable daily speaking with feedback on a few recurring mistakes, rather than trying to correct everything at once.
items.ideaZh: 经常用语言表达真实想法、倾听并发现不足；边练边纠正少量反复错误，别等句句完美才开口。

items.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of AI?
items.questionZh: 人工智能有哪些优点和缺点？
items.answer: AI can help people draft ideas, organise information and get a first explanation of something unfamiliar. The main difficulty is that a confident answer may still be wrong. There are also concerns about private information and depending on it too much. I'd treat it as a tool whose output needs judgment, especially for important decisions.
items.ideaZh: 可帮助构思、整理信息和初步理解陌生内容；回答可能自信但错误，还涉及隐私及依赖，应结合判断使用。

items.question: Do you think people today should learn about AI technology?
items.questionZh: 现在的人应该了解人工智能技术吗？
items.answer: Yes, at least the basics. People don't all need to build AI systems, but understanding what these tools can and cannot do helps them use them sensibly. They should know that an answer needs checking and that sharing personal information has consequences. Basic awareness matters more than learning complicated technical terms.
items.ideaZh: 至少了解基础能力与局限、核实回答和保护个人信息；不必人人开发系统或记复杂术语。

items.question: Should children learn to use AI?
items.questionZh: 孩子应该学习使用人工智能吗？
items.answer: They can learn about it with age-appropriate guidance. For example, a teacher could compare an AI answer with a reliable source and discuss mistakes. Children still need to practise thinking and writing themselves. The goal should be understanding the tool, rather than making it the automatic answer to every school task.
items.ideaZh: 可以在适龄指导下，把 AI 回答与可靠来源比较；孩子仍要自己思考写作，目标是理解工具而非所有任务都依赖它。

items.question: How can AI help in our lives?
items.questionZh: 人工智能能怎样帮助我们的生活？
items.answer: It can support tasks such as planning a first draft, suggesting practice questions or explaining an unfamiliar idea in simpler language. That may save time, but users still need to check important details. The most useful approach is to start with a clear need and judge whether the result actually meets it.
items.ideaZh: 辅助起草、提供练习问题、简化陌生概念，可能节省时间；先明确需求，再核查重要细节和结果是否适用。

items.question: Do you think students are overly reliant on AI?
items.questionZh: 学生是否过度依赖人工智能？
items.answer: Some may be, especially if they submit answers they cannot explain. Others use it to ask questions and then work independently. I wouldn't label all students the same. A useful test is whether someone can still discuss the idea or solve a similar problem after putting the tool away.

items.question: What can teachers do to stop students from relying too much on AI?
items.questionZh: 老师怎样防止学生过度依赖人工智能？
items.answer: They can ask students to explain their process, discuss their choices and complete some tasks independently. Clear rules about acceptable use also help. Simply banning a tool may not teach good judgment. Students need to understand why doing the thinking matters and how to check information rather than copy it blindly.
items.ideaZh: 要求解释过程与选择、完成独立任务，并明确可接受用法；比单纯禁止更重要的是教会思考和核查。

items.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of advertisements?
items.questionZh: 广告有哪些优点和缺点？
items.answer: Advertisements introduce products and can help people discover useful options. They also support some media and services. On the negative side, repeated messages can be annoying, and exaggerated claims may lead people to buy things they don't need. Clear information is more helpful than pressure or promises that are difficult to judge.
items.ideaZh: 介绍产品、帮助发现选择，也支持部分媒体服务；但重复信息扰人，夸大宣传可能引发不必要消费。

items.question: Why are many advertisements endorsed by celebrities? How useful are they?
items.questionZh: 为什么很多广告请名人代言？效果怎么样？
items.answer: A familiar face can attract attention and make a product easier to remember. Fans may also connect their feelings about the celebrity with the brand. But the effect has limits. If the person seems unrelated to the product or the product disappoints customers, celebrity attention alone won't create lasting trust.
items.ideaZh: 熟悉的面孔吸引注意、方便记忆，粉丝也可能把好感转移给品牌；但人选不合适或产品不好，就难维持信任。

items.question: What is the most important factor in an advertisement?
items.questionZh: 广告中最重要的因素是什么？
items.answer: I think a clear, believable message matters most. People should understand what the product offers and why it might be useful. A funny scene or a famous person can help them notice it, but those details achieve little if viewers remember the entertainment and have no idea what was being advertised.
items.ideaZh: 信息清楚可信，让观众知道产品提供什么、为何有用；只记得笑点或明星却不记得产品，效果有限。

items.question: Why are some advertisements boring?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些广告很无聊？
items.answer: They may repeat the same message too often or take too long to make a simple point. Some also use familiar ideas without explaining anything useful. What feels boring depends on the audience, though. A practical advertisement could interest someone who needs the product and mean little to everyone else.

items.question: Is advertising important for a company? Why?
items.questionZh: 广告对公司重要吗？为什么？
items.answer: It can be important because customers need to know a business exists and what it offers. However, advertising works best alongside reliable products and service. A company that attracts people once but disappoints them will struggle to keep customers, no matter how much attention its advertisements receive.
items.ideaZh: 有助于让顾客知道公司和产品，但必须配合可靠的产品服务，否则吸引一次也留不住顾客。

items.question: Which is more effective, online advertising or offline advertising?
items.questionZh: 线上广告与线下广告哪个更有效？
items.answer: It depends on the audience and the purpose. Online advertising can reach people who are already interested in a topic, while a sign near a shop reaches people who can visit immediately. I'd judge effectiveness by useful results, such as suitable customers, rather than simply counting how many times a message appears.
items.ideaZh: 看受众和目的：线上触达感兴趣的人，店边招牌吸引附近顾客；用合适顾客等实际结果判断，不只数曝光。

items.question: Where do people in your country often go for holidays?
items.questionZh: 你们国家的人经常去哪里度假？
items.answer: People choose different destinations, including coastal places, historic cities and areas with mountain scenery. Some travel far, while others prefer a short break near home. For example, a trip within Hainan can suit someone who wants time by the sea without organising a long journey. Budget and available days influence the choice.

items.question: What is the ideal length for a holiday?
items.questionZh: 理想的假期应该多长？
items.answer: There isn't one ideal length. A weekend can be enough for a nearby place, while a longer journey needs more time to feel relaxing. I'd rather have enough space in the schedule to enjoy a few activities than extend the trip just to rush through a larger number of destinations.
items.ideaZh: 没有统一长度，附近游周末可能足够，长途需更久；宁愿留时间享受少量活动，也不为赶更多地方而延长。

items.question: How do people usually plan holidays?
items.questionZh: 人们通常怎样安排假期？
items.answer: They often start with their available dates and budget, then compare destinations and transport. Advice from friends and online information can help with accommodation and activities. I think it is useful to agree on priorities with travelling companions early, because people may have different ideas about what makes a good holiday.
items.ideaZh: 先确定日期和预算，再比目的地交通、参考朋友和网络信息；早与同伴确认重点，避免对假期的期待不同。

items.question: Is it important to plan a holiday ahead?
items.questionZh: 提前安排假期重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, for the essentials, especially transport and somewhere to stay. Planning can reduce uncertainty and avoid wasting time after arrival. But every hour doesn't need an activity. Leaving some free time gives people the chance to rest or enjoy something they discover unexpectedly during the trip.
items.ideaZh: 交通住宿等必要事项应先安排，减少不确定与到达后浪费时间；也要留空闲休息或体验意外发现。

items.question: Why do many countries try to attract people to visit?
items.questionZh: 为什么许多国家想吸引游客？
items.answer: Visitors spend money on accommodation, food, transport and activities, which can support local jobs. Tourism can also introduce a country's culture to more people. However, attracting larger numbers should be balanced with residents' needs and the condition of local places, so a popular destination remains pleasant to live in and visit.
items.ideaZh: 游客消费支持本地工作，也传播文化；但数量增长要与居民需求、环境状况平衡，保持宜居宜游。

items.question: How do people decide when to travel?
items.questionZh: 人们怎样决定旅行时间？
items.answer: They consider work or school schedules, the weather and the cost of the trip. Some choose a festival or event, while others avoid busy periods. Travelling companions matter too. Even if one person has plenty of free time, a shared trip needs dates that work for everyone involved.
items.ideaZh: 结合工作学习、天气费用、节日及旺季偏好；共同旅行还需协调所有人的空闲日期。

items.topic: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
items.question: Do Chinese people like to visit others’ homes?
items.questionZh: 中国人喜欢去别人家做客吗？
items.answer: Some do, especially when they know the host well or want to spend time with relatives. Others prefer meeting in a restaurant because it involves less preparation. It depends on the relationship and the occasion. Visiting a close family member feels different from inviting a new acquaintance into someone's private space.

items.topic: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
items.question: What do Chinese people do when they visit others?
items.questionZh: 中国人去别人家做客时通常做什么？
items.answer: People may share food, drink tea and talk about what has been happening in their lives. At a family gathering, they might also help prepare or clear the meal. I think a good guest pays attention to the host's routine, rather than expecting every home visit to follow exactly the same customs.
items.ideaZh: 分享食物、喝茶、聊近况，也可能帮忙准备或收拾；应留意主人习惯，不假定每家习俗都一样。

items.question: What kind of place do people in your country like to live in?
items.questionZh: 你们国家的人喜欢住在什么样的地方？
items.answer: Preferences vary, but convenience, comfort and affordability are common concerns. Someone working in a city may choose an apartment near transport, while another person values a quieter place with more space. Family needs can change the choice too. A suitable home is one that works for the people actually living there.

items.topic: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
items.question: What's the difference between homes in cities and those in the countryside?
items.questionZh: 城市住宅和乡村住宅有什么不同？
items.answer: City homes are often closer together and may be apartments, while some countryside homes have more outdoor space. Access to work, shops and transport can differ too. These are broad patterns, though. A large city has varied neighbourhoods, and rural homes aren't all the same size or style.

items.question: What kind of gifts do people usually bring when they visit others?
items.questionZh: 去别人家做客通常带什么礼物？
items.answer: Fruit, snacks or something the host enjoys can be suitable. The relationship and occasion matter more than spending a lot. items.question: How often do you visit your relatives or friends?
items.questionZh: 你多久拜访一次亲戚或朋友？
items.answer: I meet friends fairly regularly, although we often go out rather than visit each other's homes. Family visits happen when our schedules allow, especially around a gathering. I prefer a relaxed visit with time to talk, rather than dropping in unexpectedly when someone might already be busy.

items.question: Should schools teach children about animals?
items.questionZh: 学校应该教孩子有关动物的知识吗？
items.answer: Yes, children should learn about animals' needs and how to treat them responsibly. Lessons can also explain the difference between a pet and a wild animal. Stories may create interest, but factual learning matters too, so children don't expect a real animal to behave like a character in a cartoon.
items.ideaZh: 应该，了解动物需求、负责任对待，区分宠物与野生动物；故事可激趣，但真实动物不等于卡通角色。

items.question: Some people think pets should not be kept in cities. What do you think?
items.questionZh: 有人认为城市不应该养宠物，你怎么看？
items.answer: I wouldn't support a complete ban. Some pets can live well in cities if owners provide suitable care and consider neighbours. The important questions are the animal's needs, available space and responsible behaviour. Keeping an animal without enough time or ability to care for it is a problem wherever someone lives.
items.ideaZh: 不赞成全面禁止；关键是提供适当照顾、空间并顾及邻居，任何地方都不应在无能力照顾时养宠物。

items.question: Many people regard pets as members of their family. What do you think?
items.questionZh: 许多人把宠物当家人，你怎么看？
items.answer: I understand it, because caring for an animal every day can create a strong bond. Pets may become part of a family's routines and memories. items.question: Do many people keep pets in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家养宠物的人多吗？
items.answer: I see people with pets, especially dogs and cats, in everyday life, but I don't know the national proportion. items.question: What are the advantages of keeping a pet?
items.questionZh: 养宠物有什么好处？
items.answer: A pet can provide companionship and a shared focus for family members. Looking after one can also encourage a regular routine. But those benefits come with responsibility and ongoing costs. Someone should choose a pet because they can meet its needs, rather than only expecting it to make their own life more enjoyable.
items.ideaZh: 提供陪伴、家庭共同关注的话题并促进规律生活；但伴随责任和持续费用，应先有能力满足动物需求。

items.question: Why do people always tell children stories with animals?
items.questionZh: 为什么人们总给孩子讲动物故事？
items.answer: Animals can make a story memorable, especially when their different characteristics help illustrate an idea. A slow tortoise and a fast hare create a clear contrast, for example. But people don't only tell animal stories. It is one useful way to explore feelings and choices in a form children can follow.

items.question: Do you think smart children are happier than other children?
items.questionZh: 聪明的孩子比其他孩子更快乐吗？
items.answer: Not necessarily. Learning quickly may make some school tasks easier, but happiness also depends on friendship, support and expectations. A child who feels constant pressure to be the best may not feel happy at all. I'd avoid assuming that one kind of ability tells us everything about a child's experience.
items.ideaZh: 未必，学得快或让学业容易些，但幸福也取决于友情、支持与期待；持续争第一的压力可能损害快乐。

items.question: Is it important for schools to identify and develop each student’s talents?
items.questionZh: 学校发现并培养每个学生的天赋重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, schools should offer chances to discover different strengths, including practical, artistic and social abilities. However, identifying talent shouldn't become a fixed label. Children develop at different rates. A student who hasn't shown an obvious strength yet still deserves encouragement and opportunities to try unfamiliar activities.

items.question: Do you think children are born smart or they learn to become smart?
items.questionZh: 孩子的聪明是天生的还是后天学来的？
items.answer: I think natural differences and experience both play a part. Children can develop knowledge, strategies and confidence through learning and practice. Rather than focusing only on whether someone was born smart, schools can help each child ask better questions, try different approaches and learn from feedback.

items.question: How do children become smart at school?
items.questionZh: 孩子怎样在学校变得更聪明？
items.answer: They develop their thinking by asking questions, solving problems and explaining their ideas. Teachers can help them compare methods instead of memorising only one answer. Working with classmates can also reveal different approaches. Improvement is easier when mistakes lead to useful feedback rather than a label about the child's ability.

items.question: Why are some people well-rounded and others only good at one thing?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人全面发展，有人只擅长一件事？
items.answer: People have different interests, opportunities and ways of spending their time. Someone may practise one activity deeply, while another enjoys exploring several areas. Neither pattern is automatically better. Specialists offer depth, and people with broader experience may connect ideas across tasks. Many groups benefit from having both.

items.question: Why does modern society need talents of all kinds?
items.questionZh: 现代社会为什么需要各种人才？
items.answer: Society has many different needs, from repairing equipment and providing care to designing software and creating art. No single kind of ability can meet all of them. items.question: What kinds of rules do schools in China have?
items.questionZh: 中国学校有哪些规则？
items.answer: Rules vary by school, but common examples involve attendance, classroom behaviour, safety and completing work honestly. Some schools also have expectations about uniforms or phone use. items.question: Do you think school rules are important?
items.questionZh: 学校规则重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, reasonable rules make learning and sharing space easier. Students need to know that others won't continually interrupt or treat them unfairly. However, rules should be clear and reasonable. If they focus on minor details while ignoring real problems, students may stop seeing them as useful.

items.question: Are children unhappy with the school rules?

items.answer: Some rules can be unpopular, especially when students don't understand the reason or feel they are applied unfairly. items.question: How can parents and teachers help children understand and follow rules?
items.questionZh: 家长和老师怎样帮助孩子理解并遵守规则？
items.answer: They can explain the purpose with everyday examples and behave consistently themselves. Children should be able to ask questions without being treated as deliberately difficult. When a rule is broken, discussing what happened and how to put it right can teach more than a punishment with no explanation.

items.question: What are the rules people should obey at work?
items.questionZh: 人们在工作中应该遵守哪些规则？
items.answer: People should follow safety procedures, respect colleagues and handle information responsibly. They also need to be reliable about agreed tasks and working times. Specific rules depend on the job. A good workplace explains expectations clearly and makes it possible to raise concerns when a rule or instruction seems unclear.

items.question: What is the purpose of punishment?
items.questionZh: 惩罚的目的是什么？
items.answer: The purpose should be to discourage harmful behaviour, protect others and help prevent the same problem happening again. It should be fair and connected to what happened. In a school, for example, a consequence is more useful when a child understands the harm and how to repair it, rather than simply feels embarrassed.
items.ideaZh: 阻止有害行为、保护他人并预防重犯；应公平且与行为相关，帮助理解伤害和补救，而非只让人难堪。

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: In what situations do people spend a long time responding to others’ messages?
items.questionZh: 什么情况下人们会很久才回复消息？
items.answer: They may be working, studying or dealing with something that needs their full attention. Sometimes they need to check information before giving a useful answer. A delayed reply doesn't automatically show a lack of respect. It helps if an urgent message clearly explains when an answer is needed.
items.ideaZh: 可能在工作学习或专注处理其他事，也可能要先核查信息；延迟不必然是不尊重，急事应说明回复期限。

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: In what situations do people not respond to messages at all?
items.questionZh: 什么情况下人们完全不回复消息？
items.answer: They might miss the message, forget after reading it or decide it doesn't require an answer. Unwanted advertising is another case. Occasionally someone avoids a difficult conversation, but we shouldn't assume that immediately. The relationship, the content and whether the message reached the right person all matter.
items.ideaZh: 可能漏看、看后忘记、认为无需回复或是垃圾广告；也可能回避难聊的话题，但不能立刻这样推断。

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: What would you do if you did not receive a reply after sending out a message?
items.questionZh: 发消息后没收到回复，你会怎么办？
items.answer: I'd consider how urgent it was. For a casual plan, I'd wait and send one polite follow-up later. If I needed an answer quickly, I might call. Sending repeated messages without considering the other person's situation would probably create more pressure without making the conversation clearer.
items.ideaZh: 不急的安排先等，稍后礼貌跟进一次；急事可以打电话，不顾对方处境反复催促只会增加压力。

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: Why do some people prefer sending a message instead of making a call?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人喜欢发消息而不是打电话？
items.answer: A message lets them explain the point without interrupting someone immediately. The other person can reply when they are free, and written details are easy to check later. A call may be better for something urgent or complicated, but not every everyday question needs an instant conversation.
items.ideaZh: 不立即打断对方，对方有空再回，文字细节便于复查；紧急复杂情况则可能更适合通话。

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: How do you show your respect in your messages?
items.questionZh: 你怎样在消息中表达尊重？
items.answer: I keep the purpose clear, use a suitable greeting and say thank you when someone helps. I also consider whether I'm messaging at a reasonable time. Respect isn't only about formal words; it includes not demanding an immediate reply to a question that can comfortably wait.
items.ideaZh: 目的清楚、合适问候、感谢帮助并注意发送时间；尊重也包含不强求对方立刻回答不急的问题。

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: Why do some people feel angry when others don’t reply to their message?
items.questionZh: 为什么别人不回复时有些人会生气？
items.answer: They may interpret the silence as being ignored, especially if they expected a quick answer. That feeling can be stronger when a plan depends on the reply. But expectations often differ. Agreeing on a deadline for important messages is more useful than assuming everyone checks their phone in the same way.
items.ideaZh: 可能把沉默理解为忽视，尤其安排依赖回复时；双方期待可能不同，重要消息宜约定期限。

items.question: Why should children have ambitions?
items.questionZh: 为什么孩子应该有志向？
items.answer: An ambition can give children a reason to learn and something to work towards. It also helps them connect effort with progress. However, their ambitions should be allowed to change as they discover new interests. A childhood goal is a starting point, not a promise they must keep for the rest of their lives.
items.ideaZh: 目标让学习有方向、把努力和进步联系起来；但允许随新兴趣调整，童年目标不是终身承诺。
items.vocab: ambition — 志向；work towards — 为……努力

items.question: What do you think of people going after high positions?
items.questionZh: 你怎么看追求高职位的人？
items.answer: It can be positive if they want to take responsibility and contribute more. The problem is when the title matters more than the work or the people affected. I'd judge the way someone pursues the position: developing useful skills is very different from undermining colleagues simply to move ahead.
items.ideaZh: 愿意担责贡献是积极的，但不能只重头衔；应看追求方式，提升技能与打压同事完全不同。

items.question: Why are some young people keen on being fans of superstars?
items.questionZh: 为什么一些年轻人热衷追星？
items.answer: They may admire a person's talent, style or story, and sharing that interest can help them connect with friends. A successful athlete might also inspire them to practise. Admiration becomes less useful if it takes too much time or replaces their own goals, so some balance is important.
items.ideaZh: 欣赏才华、风格或经历，也借共同兴趣交朋友，运动员还能激励练习；但不应挤占时间或取代自身目标。
items.vocab: admiration — 欣赏、崇拜；inspire — 激励

items.question: Is it good for a person to be ambitious?
items.questionZh: 有抱负是好事吗？
items.answer: Usually, ambition can encourage effort and help someone keep going through difficulties. But it needs realistic steps and consideration for other people. Wanting to improve is useful; believing that nothing matters except reaching one position can make ordinary progress feel disappointing. I think flexible ambition is easier to sustain.
items.ideaZh: 通常促进努力和坚持，但需要现实步骤、顾及他人；只认一个职位会否定普通进步，灵活的目标更可持续。
items.vocab: sustain — 维持；realistic — 切合实际的

items.question: Do you think it is necessary to be ambitious when working in a team in a company?
items.questionZh: 公司团队成员有抱负是必要的吗？
items.answer: Some ambition helps because team members need to care about doing good work and improving. It doesn't have to mean everyone wants to lead. A person can aim to become more reliable or skilled in their role. Team ambition works best when personal progress supports the shared result.
items.ideaZh: 适度追求做好工作和进步有益，不必人人争当领导；也可提升可靠性与技能，让个人进步支持共同成果。

items.question: Should parents support their children in pursuing their ambitions?
items.questionZh: 父母应该支持孩子追求志向吗？
items.answer: Yes, by listening, providing guidance and helping children understand the practical steps. Support doesn't have to mean agreeing that every goal will happen exactly as imagined. Parents can encourage exploration while discussing time, cost and alternatives. That helps children make informed choices without feeling their interests have been dismissed.
items.ideaZh: 应倾听、指导并帮助理解实际步骤；支持不等于保证所有愿望实现，可一起讨论时间、费用及替代方案。

items.question: When do most children begin to have their own opinions?
items.questionZh: 大多数孩子什么时候开始有自己的观点？
items.answer: They show preferences quite early, for example about food or activities, but more developed opinions grow with experience and language. I wouldn't choose one exact age. Adults can help by asking children why they think something and taking the answer seriously, while still providing guidance and new information.
items.ideaZh: 很早就会表现食物活动偏好，更完整观点随语言和经验发展；不指定统一年龄，成人可认真听理由并指导。

items.question: Whose opinions are more important to children, their parents' or teachers'?
items.questionZh: 对孩子来说，父母还是老师的意见更重要？
items.answer: It depends on the subject and the relationship. A child may trust a teacher's advice about schoolwork and a parent's advice about family matters. Sometimes the opinions conflict, which can be confusing. It helps when adults explain their reasons rather than expecting the child to choose a side automatically.
items.ideaZh: 取决于主题和关系，学业可能信老师，家庭事务可能信父母；意见冲突时应解释理由，不逼孩子盲目站队。

items.question: Do children communicate more with teachers or with parents?
items.questionZh: 孩子与老师还是父母沟通更多？
items.answer: That varies with age, daily routines and how comfortable the child feels. They may spend many hours at school but have more personal conversations at home. Time together isn't the same as meaningful communication. What matters is having a trusted adult who listens when the child needs to talk.
items.ideaZh: 取决于年龄、作息和自在程度；在校时间长不等于深度交流更多，关键是有愿意倾听的可信成人。

items.question: Who do young people like to share opinions with?
items.questionZh: 年轻人喜欢和谁分享观点？
items.answer: Often with friends who share their interests and understand their current situation. They may also turn to family or teachers for experience. The topic matters: someone might discuss a film with friends and a study decision with a teacher. Feeling listened to usually makes sharing easier.
items.ideaZh: 常与兴趣相投的朋友聊，也向家人老师寻求经验；电影和学业决定可找不同对象，被倾听更愿分享。

items.question: How does technology affect the law?
items.questionZh: 科技如何影响法律？
items.answer: Technology creates situations that existing rules may not address clearly, such as how personal data is collected or how online services treat users. It can also help people access legal information. The challenge is updating rules thoughtfully, so they protect people without becoming unclear every time a new tool appears.
items.ideaZh: 新技术带来原有规则未明确覆盖的问题，如数据收集与线上服务，也方便获取法律信息；更新规则需周全、清晰。

items.question: What kinds of rules do schools in China have?
items.questionZh: 中国学校有哪些规则？
items.answer: Common areas include attendance, safety, respectful behaviour and honest schoolwork. Details differ between schools, especially around phones and shared facilities. I think a useful rule tells students what to do and why. Consistent explanations are easier to follow than a long list that changes depending on the teacher.
items.ideaZh: 出勤、安全、尊重他人和作业诚信较常见，手机设施规定因校而异；清楚一致地说明要求与原因更容易遵守。

items.question: Will there be a law that is universally accepted?
items.questionZh: 会出现人人都接受的法律吗？
items.answer: Some broad principles, such as protecting people from harm, may gain wide support. But a specific law can still lead to disagreement about definitions, limits or enforcement. Different circumstances matter too. I think widespread acceptance is possible, while complete agreement from every person is much harder to expect.
items.ideaZh: 保护人免受伤害等原则可获广泛支持，但具体定义、边界和执行仍会有分歧；广泛认可比全员一致更现实。

items.question: What environmental laws does your country already have?
items.questionZh: 你们国家已经有哪些环境保护法律法规？
items.answer: One example I know is Hainan's rule restricting certain single-use plastic products that don't break down naturally. It took effect in December 2020. items.question: Do people read the newspaper where you live?
items.questionZh: 你住的地方有人读报纸吗？
items.answer: Some do, especially people who enjoy a familiar reading routine. Among my friends, reading news on a phone is more common. I don't think the important difference is only paper or screen. The source and whether people check the full story matter more than the format they choose.
items.ideaZh: 有些人保持读报习惯，朋友中手机看新闻更常见；来源和是否读完整报道比纸张或屏幕的形式更重要。

items.question: Do people prefer local or international news?
items.questionZh: 人们更喜欢本地还是国际新闻？
items.answer: Local news can feel immediately useful because it affects transport, services or nearby events. International news helps people understand wider issues. Many people choose a mixture, depending on what is happening. Someone may usually follow local stories but become interested in an international event that connects with their work or family.
items.ideaZh: 本地新闻贴近日常交通服务，国际新闻帮助理解更广问题；多数选择可随事件及与工作家庭的关联而变。

items.question: Do you think it's important to have a national identity?
items.questionZh: 有国家认同感重要吗？
items.answer: It can give people a sense of belonging and a connection with shared history and culture. But it should leave room for different personal backgrounds and respectful interest in other countries. I think national identity is most positive when it encourages contribution and understanding, rather than treating outsiders as less valuable.
items.ideaZh: 能带来归属感和历史文化联系，也应容纳不同背景并尊重他国；积极认同应促进贡献与理解。

items.question: How can people develop their national identity?
items.questionZh: 人们怎样培养国家认同感？
items.answer: They can learn history, take part in cultural activities and understand the lives of people from different parts of their country. Talking with older relatives can make that connection personal. It also helps to think critically about both achievements and difficulties, so belonging is based on understanding rather than only slogans.
items.ideaZh: 学历史、参加文化活动、了解各地生活及听长辈经历；同时思考成就与困难，让归属建立在理解上。
items.vocab: critically — 有辨析地；slogans — 口号

items.question: Do you think it is good to change one’s daily routine?
items.questionZh: 改变日常作息是好事吗？
items.answer: Yes, if the current routine no longer fits someone's needs or has become unhelpful. A small change can make time for a new goal. However, changing everything at once is difficult to maintain. I'd try one adjustment, see how it works and keep the parts of the old routine that remain useful.
items.ideaZh: 不再适合需求时，适度改变可给新目标腾时间；避免一次全改，先试一处调整，保留有效部分。

items.question: Do you think it is good to change jobs?
items.questionZh: 换工作是好事吗？
items.answer: It can be good when a new job offers better conditions, learning opportunities or a closer match with someone's interests. But changing only because of one difficult week may not solve the problem. People should compare the reasons carefully and understand the new role before deciding.
items.ideaZh: 条件、学习机会或兴趣匹配更好时有益；不能因一周不顺就冲动作决定，应比较原因并了解新岗位。

items.question: Is it good for people to get a job promotion?
items.questionZh: 升职是好事吗？
items.answer: Usually it can bring recognition, higher pay or a chance to develop. But it may also involve responsibilities the person doesn't enjoy, such as managing a team instead of doing specialist work. A promotion is most useful when the role fits their goals and they receive enough support to succeed.
items.ideaZh: 通常带来认可、收入和发展，也可能增加不喜欢的管理职责；岗位符合目标且有支持时才更有益。
items.vocab: recognition — 认可；specialist work — 专业性工作

items.question: Do people often make plans around their regular routines?
items.questionZh: 人们常围绕固定作息安排计划吗？
items.answer: Yes, because routines provide a clear starting point. People often arrange a social activity after work or study because those hours are already committed. However, important new plans may require changing the routine itself. Planning helps people see whether there is genuinely enough time, rather than just hoping everything will fit.
items.ideaZh: 固定工作学习时段是规划起点，因此常在之后约活动；重要新计划也可能要求调整作息，应确认真有时间。
items.vocab: committed — 已安排给某项事务的；genuinely — 确实

items.question: Who tend to change their daily routine more, young people or old people?
items.questionZh: 年轻人还是老年人更常改变日常作息？
items.answer: Young people may face more changes connected with education, work or moving home. Older people sometimes have more established routines. But personal circumstances matter more than a simple age rule. Retirement, caring responsibilities or a new interest can lead an older person to change daily life quite significantly.
items.ideaZh: 年轻人可能因升学、工作搬家变化多，老年人习惯较稳定；但退休、照护责任和新兴趣也能带来大改变，不能只看年龄。
items.vocab: retirement — 退休；established routines — 已形成的固定作息
